name: 30A (Santa Rosa Beach)
blurb: Sugar white sand, rare coastal dune lakes and small beach towns strung along Scenic Highway 30A.
day: You bike the Timpoochee Trail for coffee in Seaside, paddle a dune lake before the wind picks up, and end the day on the sand at Grayton Beach.
airport: Northwest Florida Beaches (ECP) or Destin Fort Walton (VPS)
watch: Peak season traffic, HOA rules, hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Seaside
pick_todo.note: The New Urbanist town where The Truman Show was filmed, with a walkable town center and food trucks.

pick_todo.name: Grayton Beach State Park
pick_todo.note: 2,220 acres of beach, nature trails and coastal dune lakes.

pick_todo.name: Coastal dune lakes
pick_todo.note: Rare brackish lakes that sometimes open to the Gulf. Great for paddleboarding.

pick_todo.name: Timpoochee Trail
pick_todo.note: A paved path linking the 30A communities for biking, running and walking.

name: Destin
blurb: A harbor town built around fishing charters and emerald water.
day: You're on a charter boat out of the harbor at dawn and back at a dockside table by lunch.
watch: Summer crowds, hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Destin Harbor
pick_todo.note: Charter fishing, boardwalk dining and sunset cruises.

pick_meet.name: Destin Commons Market
pick_meet.note: Growers, bakers and makers with live music on the first and third Saturday afternoons of the month.

pick_meet.name: Destin Fishing Rodeo
pick_meet.note: A month long tournament every October. 2026 is the 78th year, with free daily weigh ins on the docks behind AJ's.

pick_meet.name: Destin Pickleball Courts
pick_meet.note: Four free public courts next to the City Hall Annex, opened in September 2026. First come, first served, 8am to sunset.

pick_meet.name: Concerts in the Village
pick_meet.note: Thursday evening lawn concerts at the Mattie Kelly Arts Foundation. The 2026 season ran from April into June.

pick_meet.name: Destin Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: Three days of food, vendors and music on the Harbor Boardwalk each fall.

name: Panama City Beach
blurb: Big beaches, big energy and a lot going on after dark.
day: You spend the day on wide white sand and the evening at a live music spot near the pier.
watch: Spring break crowds, hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: St. Andrews State Park
pick_todo.note: Jetties, clear water and a quiet side of town.

pick_meet.name: Aaron Bessant Park markets
pick_meet.note: Seasonal one day farmers markets in spring, fall and December, 10am to 2pm.

pick_meet.name: Summer Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Thursday night concerts at the Aaron Bessant Park amphitheater from June through August.

pick_meet.name: Lyndell Center pickleball
pick_meet.note: Four free outdoor courts, open year round from dawn to dusk. First come, first served.

pick_meet.name: St. Andrews State Park ranger programs
pick_meet.note: Guided hikes and nature programs on the park calendar through the fall.

pick_meet.name: Ironman Florida
pick_meet.note: A long running triathlon each November. Race week is a good time to volunteer or cheer along the course.

name: Apalachicola
blurb: An oyster town with brick storefronts, shrimp boats and no hurry at all.
day: You walk to breakfast past the shrimp boats, browse the old brick downtown and watch the sun set over the bay.
watch: Storm surge and flooding in low areas

pick_todo.name: Historic downtown
pick_todo.note: Brick storefronts from the town's cotton and oyster days.

pick_todo.name: St. George Island
pick_todo.note: A quiet barrier island beach just across the bridge.

name: Cedar Key
blurb: A tiny island town of clam farms, kayaks and sunsets over the Gulf.
day: You kayak the backwater keys in the morning and eat clams on the dock at sunset.
watch: Hit hard by recent hurricanes; check rebuilding and flood zones. The nearest full grocery store is about 40 minutes away

pick_todo.name: Dock Street
pick_todo.note: Waterfront seafood and sunset views.

pick_meet.name: Cedar Key Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: Two days of seafood, crafts, live music and a Saturday parade. October 17 and 18 in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Cedar Key Arts Center
pick_meet.note: A nonprofit that runs art classes, shows and programs.

pick_meet.name: Cedar Keys Audubon
pick_meet.note: Regular sessions at the library, plus bird rescue and conservation work.

pick_meet.name: Cedar Key Lions Club
pick_meet.note: The service club that organizes the Seafood Festival.

pick_meet.name: Old Florida Celebration of the Arts
pick_meet.note: A juried art festival held every spring since 1964. The next one is April 3 and 4, 2027.

name: Dunedin
blurb: A walkable, laid back downtown near some of the Gulf's best island beaches.
day: You walk downtown for coffee, take the ferry to Caladesi Island for the beach, and bike the Pinellas Trail home.
watch: Storm surge near the water

pick_todo.name: Caladesi Island
pick_todo.note: A barrier island beach reached by ferry.

pick_todo.name: Pinellas Trail
pick_todo.note: A long paved trail running right through downtown.

pick_meet.name: Dunedin Downtown Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays year round, with Fridays added from November through June.

pick_meet.name: Dunedin Brewery open jam
pick_meet.note: A weekly Wednesday night jam session at the brewery on Douglas Avenue.

pick_meet.name: Dunedin Boat Club
pick_meet.note: Sailing races, cruises, paddling outings and monthly meetings. Founded in 1929 and open to new members.

pick_meet.name: Dunedin Fine Art Center
pick_meet.note: Art classes and exhibits.

pick_meet.name: Dunedin Highland Games and Festival
pick_meet.note: Pipe bands, dancing and athletic contests every April.

name: Clearwater Beach
blurb: Soft white sand, a walkable beach strip and nightly sunset gatherings at Pier 60.
day: You walk the beach at sunrise and join the crowd at Pier 60 for the sunset.
watch: Visitor crowds, storm surge

pick_todo.name: Pier 60
pick_todo.note: The nightly sunset gathering spot.

pick_meet.name: Clearwater Community Sailing Center
pick_meet.note: On Sand Key, with group and private lessons and memberships that cover sailboats, kayaks and paddleboards.

pick_meet.name: Sunsets at Pier 60
pick_meet.note: A free nightly gathering with artisans and street performers, weather permitting.

pick_meet.name: Pier 60 Sugar Sand Festival
pick_meet.note: Sand sculptures, beach concerts and fireworks each spring. The next one runs March 26 to April 11, 2027.

pick_meet.name: Clearwater Beach Library and Recreation Complex
pick_meet.note: The city's library and rec center on the island.

pick_meet.name: Clearwater Jazz Holiday
pick_meet.note: Four days of music each October at Coachman Park, a ferry ride away. 2026 is its 47th year.

name: Gulfport
blurb: An artsy little waterfront town with a slow pace and a friendly main street.
day: You wander the galleries on Beach Boulevard and catch live music by the water.
watch: Flooding in low lying streets. Hit hard by Helene in 2024

pick_meet.name: Gulfport Tuesday Fresh Market
pick_meet.note: Every Tuesday, year round, on Beach Boulevard. 9am to 2pm, and until 3pm January through April.

pick_meet.name: Gulfport Night Market
pick_meet.note: First Fridays and third Saturdays, 5 to 9pm on Beach Boulevard. It replaced the Art Walk and IndieFaire.

pick_meet.name: Boca Ciega Yacht Club
pick_meet.note: Adult sailing school, Sunday and Tuesday night racing and a full social calendar.

pick_meet.name: GeckoFest
pick_meet.note: A street festival and walking parade on Beach Boulevard each Labor Day weekend. 2026 was the 26th.

pick_meet.name: Gulfport Connects
pick_meet.note: The city's volunteer portal, a quick way to find a local project to help with.

name: Anna Maria Island
blurb: Old Florida on a small island, with no high rises and a free trolley.
day: You ride the trolley to breakfast, read on a quiet beach and watch the sun drop into the Gulf.
watch: Island flooding and storm exposure

pick_todo.name: Free island trolley
pick_todo.note: Runs the length of the island.

pick_meet.name: Bradenton Runners Club
pick_meet.note: Saturday at 8am at Coquina Beach, a relaxed 2 to 4 miles.

pick_meet.name: The Center of Anna Maria Island
pick_meet.note: Adult soccer, flag football and 3v3 basketball leagues each season, plus pickleball and tennis. Fall 2026 leagues are under way.

pick_meet.name: The Island Players
pick_meet.note: Community theater at 10009 Gulf Drive in Anna Maria. The 2025 to 2026 season was its 77th.

pick_meet.name: Anna Maria Island Turtle Watch and Shorebird Monitoring
pick_meet.note: Volunteers patrol the beaches in nesting season, and the group holds a Turtle Watch Wednesday evening each fall.

pick_meet.name: BayFest
pick_meet.note: A one day street festival on Pine Avenue. The 25th annual is October 17, 2026, from 10am to 9pm.

name: Longboat Key
blurb: A quiet, polished barrier island minutes from Sarasota's arts scene.
day: You walk an uncrowded beach in the morning and head to a Sarasota show at night.
watch: Storm surge on the key

pick_todo.name: St. Armands Circle
pick_todo.note: Shops and dining just off the key.

pick_meet.name: Community Cleanup
pick_meet.note: A town organized cleanup day. The next one is Saturday, October 24, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Savor the Sounds
pick_meet.note: Outdoor concert series from the Longboat Key Chamber at the Karon Family Pavilion on the Town Center Green.

pick_meet.name: Taste of the Keys
pick_meet.note: The chamber's yearly food event and scholarship fundraiser, in its 15th year in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Longboat Key Tennis Center
pick_meet.note: The town's public tennis center, open to anyone.

pick_meet.name: Let's Talk Longboat
pick_meet.note: A monthly open session hosted by the town. It is on the town calendar through early 2027.

name: Captiva Island
blurb: A small, lush island known for shelling, sunsets and slowing down.
day: You shell at low tide, bike under the banyan trees and watch the sunset from the beach.
watch: Hit hard by Ian in 2022. Most of the village has reopened. Check flood zones

pick_todo.name: Shelling beaches
pick_todo.note: Some of the best shelling in the country, with neighboring Sanibel.

pick_meet.name: Captiva Cruises
pick_meet.note: Shared boat trips to Cayo Costa, Cabbage Key, Useppa and Boca Grande, plus dolphin and sunset cruises. Running since 1986.

pick_meet.name: SCCF Coastal Watch
pick_meet.note: Volunteer beach cleanups and mangrove and oyster restoration on Sanibel and Captiva.

pick_meet.name: Island Hopper Songwriter Fest
pick_meet.note: Ten days of songwriter shows each September, with Captiva as one of four stops.

name: Matlacha
blurb: A colorful fishing village of galleries, bait shops and bridges.
day: You fish off the bridge in the morning and browse brightly painted galleries in the afternoon.
watch: Storm damage history; check flood zones

pick_todo.name: Matlacha Pass
pick_todo.note: Kayaking and fishing through the mangroves.

pick_meet.name: Matlacha Art Walk
pick_meet.note: A monthly evening walk with vendors and live music along Pine Island Road.

pick_meet.name: Calusa Land Trust
pick_meet.note: Volunteer work parties and guided paddles on preserve land around Pine Island.

pick_meet.name: Great Calusa Blueway
pick_meet.note: A marked paddling trail through Matlacha Pass. Two outfitters in the village rent kayaks.

name: Naples
blurb: Polished and peaceful, with golf, boating, a walkable downtown and calm Gulf beaches from the pier north to Vanderbilt Beach.
day: You play a morning round, walk Fifth Avenue South for lunch and watch the sunset from the beach at the end of the street.
watch: Storm surge (Ian in 2022), summer heat

pick_todo.name: Fifth Avenue South
pick_todo.note: Walkable dining and shops.

pick_todo.name: Delnor-Wiggins Pass State Park
pick_todo.note: A mile of natural beach that often lands on best beach lists.

pick_meet.name: Third Street South Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: A Saturday morning market on Third Street South that dates to 1994.

pick_meet.name: Naples Botanical Garden
pick_meet.note: A volunteer program, plus music in the garden on select Saturdays from October through June.

pick_meet.name: Gulf Coast Runners
pick_meet.note: Group runs and races all year, including the Thanksgiving 5K at Cambier Park on November 26, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Evening on Fifth
pick_meet.note: Live music along the sidewalks of Fifth Avenue South. Fall 2026 dates include October 8 and November 12.

pick_meet.name: Art in the Park
pick_meet.note: An outdoor art show downtown during the winter season, a Naples tradition since 1957.

pick_meet.name: Artis-Naples
pick_meet.note: A volunteer program at the home of the Naples Philharmonic and The Baker Museum.

name: Key West
blurb: The end of the road: bikes, sunsets, live music and island time.
day: You bike to coffee, spend the afternoon on the water and walk to Mallory Square for the sunset.
watch: Long evacuation route, high insurance, small lots

pick_todo.name: Mallory Square
pick_todo.note: The nightly sunset celebration.

name: Islamorada
blurb: The sport fishing capital of the Keys, laid back and on the water.
day: You're out on the flats at sunrise and at a waterfront fish house by sunset.
watch: Evacuation distance, high insurance

pick_todo.name: Backcountry flats
pick_todo.note: World famous fishing for bonefish and tarpon.

pick_meet.name: Founders Park
pick_meet.note: The village park at mile marker 87, with a pool, courts, a marina and a monthly schedule of rec programs.

pick_meet.name: Morada Way Art Walk
pick_meet.note: Third Thursday of each month on Morada Way, with art for sale, food and live music on several stages.

pick_meet.name: History of Diving Museum
pick_meet.note: Open daily at mile marker 83, with an evening talk series called Immerse Yourself.

pick_meet.name: Islamorada area state parks
pick_meet.note: Windley Key Fossil Reef and Lignumvitae Key are open Thursday through Monday, and Florida State Parks takes volunteers.

pick_meet.name: Florida Keys Overseas Heritage Trail
pick_meet.note: The paved path along US 1 where walkers, runners and cyclists cross paths.

name: Miami (South Beach)
blurb: Art deco, ocean views and a city that never slows down.
day: You run the beachwalk at sunrise, work from a cafe and head out to dinner late.
watch: Flooding, traffic, high insurance

pick_todo.name: Art Deco District
pick_todo.note: Historic architecture along Ocean Drive.

pick_meet.name: Lincoln Road Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Every Sunday, 9am to 6pm, year round, between Meridian and Washington avenues.

pick_meet.name: Free community yoga on Lincoln Road
pick_meet.note: A free weekly morning class on the pedestrian mall.

pick_meet.name: Art Deco Weekend
pick_meet.note: The Miami Design Preservation League's festival on Ocean Drive. The 50th runs January 15 to 17, 2027.

pick_meet.name: Art Walk on Lincoln Road
pick_meet.note: Free, on the third Thursday of every month.

pick_meet.name: WALLCAST concerts at SoundScape Park
pick_meet.note: Seven free New World Symphony concerts shown on the outdoor wall from October 2026 through May 2027.

name: Fort Lauderdale
blurb: A boating city of canals, marinas and a lively beach.
day: You take the boat out through the canals, then grab dinner on Las Olas.
watch: Flooding, high insurance

pick_todo.name: Las Olas Boulevard
pick_todo.note: Dining and shops near the river.

pick_meet.name: Sunday Jazz Brunch
pick_meet.note: Free live jazz on three stages at Esplanade Park on the Riverwalk, the first Sunday of every month from 11am to 2pm.

pick_meet.name: The LOOP weekend markets
pick_meet.note: Saturday and Sunday markets at Las Olas Oceanside Park, across from the beach.

pick_meet.name: Winterfest Boat Parade
pick_meet.note: A 12 mile holiday boat parade that signs up volunteers every year. The 2026 parade is Saturday, December 12.

pick_meet.name: Weekly run clubs
pick_meet.note: Several group runs meet downtown, on Las Olas and at breweries on weeknights. Check each club for its current schedule.

pick_meet.name: The Fort
pick_meet.note: A 43 court pickleball complex with daily clinics, social and competitive leagues and open play sorted by skill. Day passes are sold.

name: Delray Beach
blurb: A walkable downtown that runs right to the ocean and stays up late.
day: You walk Atlantic Avenue for breakfast, hit the beach at the end of the street and come back for dinner and music.
airport: Palm Beach airport or Fort Lauderdale (FLL)
watch: Traffic, higher insurance

pick_todo.name: Atlantic Avenue
pick_todo.note: Restaurants and nightlife that run to the beach.

name: Jupiter
blurb: Clear inlet water, a red lighthouse and a relaxed, outdoorsy pace.
day: You paddle the Loxahatchee River in the morning and snorkel the inlet in the afternoon.
watch: Hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse
pick_todo.note: A historic lighthouse and museum.

pick_meet.name: Harbourside Place Run Club
pick_meet.note: A weekly 5K run and walk from the amphitheater, Thursdays at 6:30pm.

pick_meet.name: The Market at Harbourside Place
pick_meet.note: Sundays from 10am to 3pm, with morning yoga by the amphitheater first.

pick_meet.name: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse & Museum
pick_meet.note: Open Tuesday through Sunday, with guided tours and sunset climbs on the calendar.

pick_meet.name: Trivia at Subculture Coffee
pick_meet.note: Wednesdays at 7pm at Harbourside Place.

pick_meet.name: Maltz Jupiter Theatre
pick_meet.note: Five mainstage shows from October through March, plus concerts.

name: Fort Pierce
blurb: An affordable working waterfront with a big Saturday market.
day: You fish the inlet in the morning and walk the downtown farmers market.
watch: Hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Fort Pierce Inlet
pick_todo.note: Fishing and beaches at the inlet park.

pick_meet.name: Downtown Fort Pierce Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday downtown, the biggest weekly gathering in town.

pick_meet.name: Friday Fest
pick_meet.note: A live music street party downtown.

pick_meet.name: Jazz Market
pick_meet.note: A recurring downtown market, a companion to the Saturday farmers market.

pick_meet.name: Art Walk
pick_meet.note: A monthly evening of open galleries and studios downtown.

pick_meet.name: Manatee Observation and Education Center
pick_meet.note: A waterfront center downtown with exhibits and lagoon views.

name: Cocoa Beach
blurb: A classic surf town where you can watch rocket launches from the sand.
day: You surf in the morning and watch a launch from the beach in the evening.
airport: Orlando (MCO), about 50 minutes, or Melbourne (MLB), about 40
watch: Hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Cocoa Beach Pier
pick_todo.note: Surfing and the classic pier.

pick_meet.name: Friday Fest
pick_meet.note: A downtown street party with live music and artisans the third Friday of every month.

pick_meet.name: Friday Fest & Songwriter Festival
pick_meet.note: A free weekend of songwriters and live music across six venues, October 16 to 18, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Sip & Stroll
pick_meet.note: Ticketed evening walks through downtown run by Cocoa Beach Main Street. One is set for October 24, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Surfin' Santas
pick_meet.note: Surfers in Santa suits take over downtown and the beach the morning of December 24.

pick_meet.name: Beachside Color Fun Run 5K
pick_meet.note: An all paces run that starts at Coconuts on the Beach. The next one is January 2, 2027.

name: New Smyrna Beach
blurb: A laid back surf town about an hour from Orlando.
day: You check the surf before breakfast and end the day with tacos on Flagler Avenue.
watch: Hurricane exposure on the barrier island

pick_todo.name: Flagler Avenue
pick_todo.note: The walkable beach strip.

pick_meet.name: New Smyrna Beach Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday morning on Sams Avenue downtown, running since 1991, with live music.

pick_meet.name: First Saturday Art & Artisan Stroll
pick_meet.note: Canal Street fills with art, antiques, sidewalk sales and live music on the first Saturday of the month.

pick_meet.name: Flagler Avenue Wine Walk
pick_meet.note: A monthly tasting stroll along the Avenue with a passport and a glass.

pick_meet.name: Coronado-Mainland Shuffleboard Club
pick_meet.note: Courts right on Flagler Avenue and friendly competition.

pick_meet.name: Marine Discovery Center
pick_meet.note: Volunteer on oyster bed and shoreline restoration projects, or join a kayak tour of the Indian River Lagoon.

name: Daytona Beach
blurb: Wide beaches and some of the most affordable coastal homes in Florida.
day: You drive onto the hard packed beach and set up for the day.
watch: Event crowds, hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Beach driving
pick_todo.note: One of the few beaches where you can drive on the sand.

pick_meet.name: Daytona Beach Bandshell concerts
pick_meet.note: Live shows at the historic oceanfront Bandshell.

pick_meet.name: Halifax Art Festival
pick_meet.note: An art festival in the Riverfront Arts District each November. In 2026 it starts November 7.

pick_meet.name: Jackie Robinson Ballpark
pick_meet.note: Baseball games at the historic downtown ballpark.

pick_meet.name: Biketoberfest
pick_meet.note: The fall motorcycle rally, held countywide each October. In 2026 it starts October 15.

pick_meet.name: ONE DAYTONA
pick_meet.note: The dining and entertainment district across from the Speedway.

name: Flagler Beach
blurb: A small, unhurried beach town along A1A, with a new pier on the way.
day: You walk the beach at sunrise and grab lunch on A1A with an ocean view.
watch: Beach erosion, hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Flagler Beach Pier
pick_todo.note: Being rebuilt as a longer pier, expected to open in early 2027.

pick_meet.name: Gamble Rogers Memorial State Recreation Area
pick_meet.note: Boat ramp, kayak launch and hammock trails at the south end of town.

pick_meet.name: Palm Coast Songwriters Festival
pick_meet.note: An annual music festival a short drive north in Palm Coast.

pick_meet.name: Southern Recreation Center
pick_meet.note: Palm Coast's tennis and pickleball center, with programs and tournaments.

pick_meet.name: Holiday Boat Parade
pick_meet.note: Decorated boats on the Intracoastal in Palm Coast each December.

name: St. Augustine
blurb: The oldest city in the country, with brick streets and beaches a bridge away.
day: You have coffee in the old town before the tour buses arrive and bike over the bridge to the beach.
watch: Low lying streets flood in big storms

pick_todo.name: Historic district
pick_todo.note: Colonial streets and the Castillo de San Marcos.

pick_meet.name: First Friday Art Walk
pick_meet.note: Almost 30 galleries open their doors on the first Friday of every month.

pick_meet.name: Amphitheatre Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Saturday mornings, 8:30 to 12:30, at the St. Augustine Amphitheatre on Anastasia Island.

pick_meet.name: Ancient City Road Runners
pick_meet.note: A Wednesday evening group run that meets behind the Lightner Museum and ends at a brewery.

pick_meet.name: Colonial Oak Music Park
pick_meet.note: Free outdoor shows under the oaks on St. George Street.

pick_meet.name: Matanzas 5000
pick_meet.note: A 5K the road runners club has put on for more than four decades.

name: Jacksonville Beach
blurb: A lively beach town with surf, patios and a big city next door.
day: You surf by the pier and meet friends for dinner a block from the sand.
watch: Hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Jacksonville Beach Pier
pick_todo.note: Surf and fishing.

pick_meet.name: Beaches Green Market
pick_meet.note: A Saturday market for local growers and makers at Jarboe Park, next door in Neptune Beach.

pick_meet.name: Players by the Sea
pick_meet.note: Community theatre in its 61st season, with open auditions and volunteer crews.

pick_meet.name: Beaches Museum
pick_meet.note: Free admission, Boardwalk Talks, chapel concerts and volunteer shifts on Beach Boulevard.

pick_meet.name: Seawalk Sessions
pick_meet.note: Live music at the Seawalk Pavilion by the ocean. The city had one on the calendar for October 2026.

pick_meet.name: Jax Beach Golf Club
pick_meet.note: The city's public golf course.

name: Fernandina Beach
blurb: A Victorian downtown, shrimp boats and quiet beaches near Georgia.
day: You walk Centre Street for coffee, watch the shrimp boats come in and spend the afternoon on an uncrowded beach.
watch: Storm surge on the island

pick_todo.name: Centre Street
pick_todo.note: A walkable Victorian downtown.

pick_meet.name: Fernandina Beach Market Place
pick_meet.note: Farmers market every Saturday, 9am to 1pm, on North 7th Street. Year round, rain or shine.

pick_meet.name: Sounds on Centre
pick_meet.note: Free outdoor concerts downtown on the first Friday of the month, April through October.

pick_meet.name: Isle of Eight Flags Shrimp Festival
pick_meet.note: The big spring weekend downtown, with volunteer roles every year. The 2026 festival was May 1 to 3.

pick_meet.name: Island Art Association
pick_meet.note: A volunteer run artist cooperative on North 2nd Street with classes and workshops.

pick_meet.name: Amelia Community Theatre
pick_meet.note: Season 46 is under way on two stages on Cedar Street, and the theatre is always signing up volunteers.

name: Carrabelle
blurb: A small fishing town on the Forgotten Coast with a working harbor and a slow, friendly pace.
day: You launch at the river before sunrise, run out toward Dog Island and are back at the marina for a late breakfast.
watch: Storm surge, few services nearby

pick_todo.name: Carrabelle Beach
pick_todo.note: A quiet stretch of Gulf sand just west of town.

pick_meet.name: Country Farmer's Market
pick_meet.note: Produce and crafts at the Crooked River Lighthouse on the first and third Saturdays, 9am to 1pm.

pick_meet.name: Carrabelle Artist Association
pick_meet.note: A group for painters, makers and anyone who wants to try.

pick_meet.name: Franklin County library clubs
pick_meet.note: Craft workshops and tech help at the Carrabelle branch, with a book club, mahjong and a writers forum in Eastpoint.

pick_meet.name: Carrabelle Riverfront Festival
pick_meet.note: A free day of music, food, quilts and classic cars on Marine Street each April.

pick_meet.name: Twilight at the Tower
pick_meet.note: Evening lighthouse climbs and museum visits at the Crooked River Lighthouse on select summer nights.

name: St. George Island
blurb: A barrier island with no high rises, a lighthouse at its center and nine miles of state park beach at the east end.
day: You bike to coffee, spend the day on the state park beach and climb the lighthouse at sunset.
watch: Storm surge on a barrier island. Michael brought at least 5 feet of it in 2018. One bridge on and off
season: Busy summers and spring break, quiet winters

pick_todo.name: St. George Island State Park
pick_todo.note: Nine miles of undeveloped beach. Dr. Beach named it number one in America in 2023.

pick_todo.name: Cape St. George Light
pick_todo.note: A 77 foot lighthouse with 92 stairs and a small museum, right where the bridge lands.

pick_meet.name: St. George Island Civic Club
pick_meet.note: The third Thursday of each month at the firehouse on East Pine. Social at 6:30pm, potluck at 7.

pick_meet.name: Sunset and Full Moon Climb
pick_meet.note: Monthly at the Cape St. George Light, $10. Fall 2026 dates include October 26 and November 24.

pick_meet.name: Charity Chili Cookoff
pick_meet.note: Early March by the lighthouse, 44 years running in 2026. It raises money for the volunteer fire department.

pick_meet.name: St. George Island Sea Turtle Patrol
pick_meet.note: A volunteer group that looks after the nests each summer.

pick_meet.name: ShrimpFest
pick_meet.note: A winter festival at the lighthouse. The next one is February 13, 2027.
