pick_todo.name: FSU Coastal and Marine Laboratory
pick_todo.note: Free guided tours on Fridays and free evening lectures open to the public.

pick_todo.name: Bald Point State Park
pick_todo.note: Two beaches and coastal trails about 20 minutes east.

pick_meet.name: Marine lab tours
pick_meet.note: Free guided tours of the FSU Coastal and Marine Laboratory on Fridays from 11 to 4.

pick_meet.name: Sopchoppy Opry
pick_meet.note: A music show on the last Saturday of each month, about 20 minutes away.

pick_meet.name: Marine lab lectures
pick_meet.note: Free public talks at 7pm, in person or online.

pick_meet.name: Marine lab volunteers
pick_meet.note: Volunteer restoration programs run through the lab's outreach office.

pick_meet.name: Carrabelle Riverfront Festival
pick_meet.note: A free day of music and food on Marine Street each April.

name: St. Marks
blurb: A tiny river town where the road ends at the water, half an hour south of Tallahassee, with a Spanish fort site, a rail trail and a huge wildlife refuge next door.
day: You ride the rail trail into town, eat lunch on the river and run the boat four miles down to the bay for the afternoon.
watch: Flooding. Storm surge has put water in town five times since 2005, most recently with Helene in 2024

pick_todo.name: St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge
pick_todo.note: More than 86,000 acres and 43 miles of coast, with a lighthouse rebuilt in 1842.

pick_todo.name: San Marcos de Apalache Historic State Park
pick_todo.note: The site of a fort begun in 1679 where the two rivers meet, with a small museum.

pick_todo.name: Tallahassee to St. Marks trail
pick_todo.note: Sixteen paved miles of old railroad that end on Riverside Drive.

pick_meet.name: St. Marks Community Market
pick_meet.note: The fourth Saturday of each month, 9am to 1pm, on Port Leon Drive.

pick_meet.name: St. Marks Stone Crab Festival
pick_meet.note: The last Saturday of October since 1997, on Port Leon Drive.

pick_meet.name: Friends of St. Marks Wildlife Refuge
pick_meet.note: Volunteers, Second Sunday speakers and a weekly trail crew that starts up in late October.

pick_meet.name: Monarch Festival
pick_meet.note: A fall day at the refuge when the butterflies pass through. The 2026 date is November 7.

pick_meet.name: Fourth of July
pick_meet.note: Vendors in the afternoon and fireworks at night.

name: Panama City
blurb: A bayfront city on St. Andrews Bay with a reviving downtown and the Gulf beaches a bridge away.
day: You grab coffee downtown, walk the marina in St. Andrews and drive 20 minutes to the beach when you feel like it.
watch: Hurricane exposure. Parts of town are still rebuilding from Michael in 2018

pick_todo.name: Historic St. Andrews
pick_todo.note: A waterfront district of seafood spots, a marina and a weekend market.

pick_meet.name: The Market at St. Andrews
pick_meet.note: A waterfront farmers market in Historic St. Andrews, just off Beck Avenue.

pick_meet.name: Backstage Pass
pick_meet.note: A fall concert series on the Marina Lawn downtown, mid September through late October. Bring a blanket or a chair.

pick_meet.name: Panama City Songwriters Festival
pick_meet.note: Two days of songwriters in venues along Harrison Avenue each November. 2026 is the eighth year.

pick_meet.name: Boat Parade of Lights
pick_meet.note: Decorated boats off the Panama City Marina each December. 2026 is the 40th.

pick_meet.name: Panama City Center for the Arts
pick_meet.note: Exhibits and seasonal events downtown, including Fright Nights each October.

name: Pensacola
blurb: Florida's westernmost city, with more than 450 years of history, a lively downtown and white sand beaches across the bay.
day: You walk Palafox Street to the Saturday market, catch a Blue Angels practice in season and watch the sunset from the bayfront.
watch: Hurricane exposure

pick_todo.name: Palafox Street
pick_todo.note: The heart of downtown, lined with restaurants, galleries and a Saturday market.

pick_meet.name: Palafox Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday from 9am to 2pm, rain or shine, at MLK Jr. Plaza and Plaza Ferdinand downtown.

pick_meet.name: Gallery Night
pick_meet.note: A downtown evening of art and music on select Fridays. The 2026 calendar includes October 16.

pick_meet.name: Pensacola Runners Association
pick_meet.note: A member club that puts on seven races a year.

pick_meet.name: Seville Quarter weeknights
pick_meet.note: Monday Night Blues open jam, Tuesday country nights with dancing, and bar bingo.

pick_meet.name: Blue Wahoos games
pick_meet.note: Minor league baseball at Blue Wahoos Stadium, an easy night out with a group.

name: Pensacola Beach
blurb: A barrier island town on Santa Rosa Island, with sugar white sand and miles of protected national seashore on both sides.
day: You bike the path along the island at sunrise, spend the day on the sand and walk to the pier for the sunset.
watch: Barrier island hurricane exposure, bridge traffic in season

pick_todo.name: Gulf Islands National Seashore
pick_todo.note: Miles of undeveloped beach and dunes on either side of town.

pick_meet.name: Bands on the Beach
pick_meet.note: Free concerts every Tuesday at 7pm at the Gulfside Pavilion. The 2026 season runs April 7 through October 27.

pick_meet.name: Pensacola Beach Air Show
pick_meet.note: The Blue Angels fly over the beach each July, and the sand fills up early to watch.

pick_meet.name: Pensacola Beach Gulf Pier
pick_meet.note: Fish or just walk out over the Gulf. The tackle shop rents gear, and it is an easy place to strike up a conversation.

pick_meet.name: Cinemas in the Sand
pick_meet.note: Outdoor movie nights on the beach, listed on the island's recurring events calendar.

name: Navarre Beach
blurb: The quiet stretch of the Emerald Coast, with a long Gulf pier, a sea turtle center and miles of open dunes between Pensacola Beach and Destin.
day: You walk the pier at sunrise to see what the anglers pulled up, swim off empty sand all day and catch live music and the sunset at Juana's on the sound.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 30 minutes. Pensacola (PNS) about 50
watch: Barrier island storm exposure. One causeway on and off the island
season: Busy April through October, calm in winter

pick_todo.name: Navarre Beach Fishing Pier
pick_todo.note: At 1,545 feet it is billed as the longest pier in the Gulf, open around the clock.

pick_meet.name: Navarre Beach Fishing Pier
pick_meet.note: Anglers chat all day out here, and it is the easiest place to meet regulars.

pick_meet.name: Sea Turtle Conservation Center
pick_meet.note: Free and run with a lot of volunteer help, which is a great way to get involved.

pick_meet.name: Juana's Pagodas
pick_meet.note: The sound side hangout for live music, kayaks and sunsets.

name: Perdido Key
blurb: A skinny barrier island on the Alabama line, with Gulf front condos, protected dunes on both ends and the Flora-Bama in the middle of it all.
day: You paddle Big Lagoon in the morning, spend the afternoon on Johnson Beach where the road runs out and end up at the Flora-Bama for a band.
watch: Barrier island hurricane exposure. Ivan and Sally both hit hard here
season: Busy summers and a packed Mullet Toss weekend in April

pick_todo.name: Johnson Beach
pick_todo.note: Miles of undeveloped national seashore at the east end of the key, with a kayak launch and boardwalks.

pick_meet.name: Flora-Bama
pick_meet.note: The famous beach bar on the state line, with live music most nights and a big regular crowd.

pick_meet.name: Interstate Mullet Toss
pick_meet.note: A huge beach party each April where people throw mullet across the state line for charity.

pick_meet.name: Big Lagoon State Park
pick_meet.note: Trails, kayak launches and a boardwalk tower over the lagoon.

name: Gulf Breeze
blurb: A leafy peninsula between downtown Pensacola and Pensacola Beach, where families come for the schools and the water is at the end of every street.
day: You drop the kids at school, walk the trails at Naval Live Oaks, take the boat out on the sound after work and are on Pensacola Beach in five minutes for sunset.
watch: Surrounded by water on three sides, so check flood zones. The Pensacola Bay Bridge was shut for months after a 2020 barge strike
season: Year round residents, busy bridge traffic on summer weekends

pick_todo.name: Naval Live Oaks
pick_todo.note: Over 1,300 acres of national seashore with live oak trails and quiet bay beaches.

pick_meet.name: Shoreline Park
pick_meet.note: Pickleball, beach volleyball, disc golf and a splash pad, so there is always someone around.

pick_meet.name: Naval Live Oaks
pick_meet.note: Trails through the oaks for regular walkers and cyclists.

pick_meet.name: Gulf Breeze Zoo
pick_meet.note: A family favorite just east of town with a safari train ride.

name: Port St. Joe
blurb: A small town on St. Joseph Bay, known for calm clear water, bay sunsets and the beaches of Cape San Blas.
day: You paddle the clear grass flats in the morning, drive out to Cape San Blas for the beach and watch the sun set over the bay.
watch: Hurricane exposure. Michael hit hard here in 2018. The state closed the 2026 scallop season in St. Joseph Bay
season: Quiet year round, busier in summer

pick_todo.name: Cape San Blas
pick_todo.note: A long, quiet peninsula of dunes and beach with a state park at the tip.

pick_meet.name: Salt Air Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Growers and makers at George Core Park on the bayfront. The fall 2026 dates run October 17 through December 19.

pick_meet.name: Friends of St. Joseph Bay Preserve
pick_meet.note: The group behind the guided tram tours of the St. Joseph Bay State Buffer Preserve.

pick_meet.name: Blast on the Bay Songwriters Festival
pick_meet.note: Songwriters play venues around Port St. Joe and the Cape each October.

pick_meet.name: Gulf County Fall Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Outdoor concerts in October at Veterans Memorial Park at Beacon Hill, a short drive up US 98.

pick_meet.name: Forgotten Coast Sea Turtle Festival
pick_meet.note: A summer festival in town built around sea turtle conservation.

name: Crystal River
blurb: A spring fed town on Kings Bay where hundreds of manatees spend the winter.
day: You paddle Kings Bay at first light with manatees surfacing around you, and in summer you head out for scallops.
watch: Storm surge flooding. Hit by recent hurricanes

pick_todo.name: Three Sisters Springs
pick_todo.note: Clear blue springs and a boardwalk for watching manatees in winter.

pick_meet.name: Crystal River Nights Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Free outdoor concerts at Town Square on select Saturdays. Bring a chair.

pick_meet.name: Stone Crab Jam
pick_meet.note: A downtown music festival on the first Saturday of November, put on by the Kings Bay Rotary Club.

pick_meet.name: Florida Manatee Festival
pick_meet.note: A big January weekend downtown with manatee boat tours, live music and seafood.

pick_meet.name: Friends of Crystal River National Wildlife Refuge Complex
pick_meet.note: The support group for the refuge that includes Three Sisters Springs.

pick_meet.name: Crystal River Preserve State Park volunteer days
pick_meet.note: Hands on habitat work, like the bioblitz and longleaf pine planting set for December 2026.

name: Homosassa
blurb: An Old Florida river town known for manatees, scalloping and waterfront spots you can pull up to by boat.
day: You idle down the Homosassa River to the Gulf for scallops and stop at a riverside spot on the way home.
watch: Storm surge flooding. Helene flooded Old Homosassa in 2024

pick_todo.name: Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park
pick_todo.note: See manatees and native Florida wildlife up close.

pick_meet.name: Homosassa Arts, Crafts and Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: A November weekend in Old Homosassa. 2025 was its 50th year.

pick_meet.name: Homosassa Civic Club
pick_meet.note: The volunteer group that puts on the Arts, Crafts and Seafood Festival.

pick_meet.name: Friends of Homosassa Springs Wildlife Park
pick_meet.note: The support group for the wildlife state park and its animals.

pick_meet.name: Wildlife park volunteers
pick_meet.note: Volunteers help staff lead the manatee and wildlife programs at the state park.

pick_meet.name: Homosassa Yukers
pick_meet.note: A ukulele group that played both mornings of the 2025 festival.

name: Ozello
blurb: A handful of homes on marsh islands at the end of a nine mile winding road. About as remote as the Gulf coast gets.
day: You launch a kayak from the back yard, fish the oyster bars and don't see another boat all morning.
watch: Very low lying and floods in storms. One winding road in and out

pick_todo.name: The Ozello Trail
pick_todo.note: A twisting road through salt marsh and hammocks that's a destination by itself.

pick_meet.name: Crystal River Nights Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Free concerts at Town Square in Crystal River on select Saturdays.

pick_meet.name: Ozello Civic Association
pick_meet.note: The community group for the islands, active for more than 50 years.

pick_meet.name: Ozello Chili Cook Off and Craft Show
pick_meet.note: The association's February fundraiser for area charities.

pick_meet.name: Ozello Community Park
pick_meet.note: The public ramp and launch where most days on the water begin.

pick_meet.name: Friends of Crystal River National Wildlife Refuge Complex
pick_meet.note: The refuge support group, based in Crystal River about half an hour away.

name: Steinhatchee
blurb: A river fishing village on the Big Bend where summer means scallops and the nearest stoplight is a long way off.
day: You run the river to the Gulf at dawn, fill a bucket with scallops and clean them on the dock.
watch: Hit hard by Idalia in 2023 and Helene in 2024. Check rebuilding and flood zones

pick_todo.name: Steinhatchee River
pick_todo.note: Marinas, fish camps and a straight shot to the grass flats.

pick_meet.name: Fiddler Crab Festival
pick_meet.note: Every Presidents Day weekend. It draws 10,000 to 15,000 people to a town with no traffic light.

pick_meet.name: Sea Hag Marina tournaments
pick_meet.note: A fishing tournament calendar that includes the Steinhatchee Open and the Nauti-Girls Tournament.

pick_meet.name: Scallop season
pick_meet.note: Mid June to Labor Day, when the ramps and docks turn into the town square.

pick_meet.name: Sips and Sunsets
pick_meet.note: A community evening held each November.

pick_meet.name: Christmas in the Park and Festival of Trees
pick_meet.note: The village holiday gathering.

name: Apollo Beach
blurb: A canal community on Tampa Bay where a lot of back yards have a boat lift.
day: You take the boat out through the canals to the bay, and in winter you stop by the manatee viewing center on the way home.
watch: Storm surge on canal homes, commuter traffic on I-75

pick_todo.name: Manatee Viewing Center
pick_todo.note: Hundreds of manatees gather in the warm water here on cold days.

pick_meet.name: Manatee Viewing Center
pick_meet.note: Free and open daily from November 1 through April 15, 10am to 5pm, with a tidal walk, a tower and a habitat trail.

pick_meet.name: Firehouse Cultural Center
pick_meet.note: Ten minutes south in Ruskin. A figure drawing group on the 2nd and 4th Thursdays, an open pottery studio, and theater, comedy and music nights.

pick_meet.name: Ruskin Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: The 36th annual is set for November 14 and 15, 2026.

pick_meet.name: SouthShore Chamber of Commerce
pick_meet.note: Covers Apollo Beach, Ruskin and Sun City Center and keeps a community calendar of parades, expos and festivals.

name: Clearwater
blurb: The mainland city behind Clearwater Beach, with a rebuilt downtown waterfront and the sand a bridge away.
day: You catch a concert at Coachman Park on the bluff, then bike the causeway to the beach.
airport: Tampa (TPA), about 30 minutes, or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE)
watch: Storm surge near the water, beach traffic

pick_todo.name: Coachman Park
pick_todo.note: A downtown waterfront park with a big outdoor concert venue.

pick_meet.name: The Market Marie
pick_meet.note: A market of local vendors at Coachman Park on the second Saturday of the month.

pick_meet.name: City adult leagues
pick_meet.note: Softball and kickball seasons run by Clearwater Parks and Recreation.

pick_meet.name: Clearwater Shuffleboard Club
pick_meet.note: Games, friendly competitions and social gatherings for all skill levels.

pick_meet.name: Clearwater Jazz Holiday
pick_meet.note: Four days at Coachman Park every October. 2026 is the 47th year.

pick_meet.name: Clearwater Threshers
pick_meet.note: Minor league baseball at BayCare Ballpark, where the Phillies also hold spring training.

name: Indian Rocks Beach
blurb: A low key beach town of cottages and small condos, with public beach access at the end of nearly every street.
day: You walk to the beach with a chair, walk home for lunch and walk back for the sunset.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE) or Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024

pick_todo.name: Beach accesses
pick_todo.note: More than two dozen public accesses, many with a little free parking.

pick_meet.name: IRB Home
pick_meet.note: A neighborhood nonprofit going since 1970, with mix and mingles, a pub crawl and Taste of IRB.

pick_meet.name: Beach Art Center
pick_meet.note: Classes and exhibits on Bay Palm Boulevard since 1978, from watercolor to jewelry making.

pick_meet.name: Oktoberfest on Indian Rocks Beach
pick_meet.note: A free afternoon at Kolb Park each October, tied to the volunteer group IRB Action 2000.

pick_meet.name: Christmas Boat Parade
pick_meet.note: Decorated boats on the Intracoastal each December. The 2026 parade is set for December 19.

name: Madeira Beach
blurb: Locals call it Mad Beach: a casual Gulf town built around the fishing boats and boardwalk at John's Pass.
day: You watch the charter boats come in at John's Pass, then cross the street to the beach.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE) or Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024

pick_todo.name: John's Pass Village
pick_todo.note: A boardwalk of seafood spots, shops and fishing charters on the inlet.

pick_meet.name: Madeira Beach Wednesday Market
pick_meet.note: Wednesdays on Madeira Way from November 2026 through May 2027, 10am to 2pm.

pick_meet.name: Trash Pirates
pick_meet.note: A volunteer beach and waterway cleanup that meets monthly at Archibald Memorial Beach Park.

pick_meet.name: Old Salt Fishing Foundation
pick_meet.note: An all volunteer group with meetings, seminars and the King of the Beach kingfish tournaments.

pick_meet.name: John's Pass Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: Three days at John's Pass each fall. The 45th runs October 23 to 25, 2026.

name: New Port Richey
blurb: A small river town with a 1920s downtown that has been adding breweries, restaurants and a restored theater.
day: You kayak the Cotee River in the morning and walk Main Street for dinner.
watch: Flooding along the river and coast

pick_todo.name: Sims Park
pick_todo.note: A riverfront park downtown with concerts and events.

pick_meet.name: Fourth Friday Bazaar
pick_meet.note: A monthly evening outdoor market downtown.

pick_meet.name: Thrive at Night Yoga
pick_meet.note: Free outdoor yoga at Cavalaire Square, listed on the Main Street calendar.

pick_meet.name: Recreation and Aquatic Center
pick_meet.note: City run programs and sports leagues.

pick_meet.name: New Port Richey Main Street
pick_meet.note: Volunteer committees that plan downtown events and meet monthly.

pick_meet.name: Chasco Fiesta
pick_meet.note: Nine days of parades and concerts, with a boat parade on the river. April 9 to 17 in 2027.

name: Ruskin
blurb: A fast growing bayside community on the Little Manatee River, with some of the lowest prices near Tampa Bay.
day: You fish the river mouth at sunrise and are home before the day heats up.
watch: Low lying areas flood. Fast growth and traffic

pick_todo.name: Little Manatee River
pick_todo.note: A quiet blackwater river for paddling and fishing.

pick_meet.name: Camp Bayou Outdoor Learning Center
pick_meet.note: A nature center at the end of 24th Street SE with a volunteer program. Open Thursday through Sunday, 9am to 2pm.

pick_meet.name: Ruskin Veterans Day Parade
pick_meet.note: Saturday, November 7 in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Firehouse Cultural Center
pick_meet.note: A figure drawing group on the 2nd and 4th Thursdays from 6 to 9pm, an open pottery studio, and theater, comedy and music series.

pick_meet.name: Ruskin Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: The 36th annual is set for November 14 and 15, 2026.

pick_meet.name: SouthShore Chamber of Commerce
pick_meet.note: Based on College Avenue in Ruskin, with a community calendar for Ruskin, Apollo Beach and Sun City Center.

name: Safety Harbor
blurb: A small town on Old Tampa Bay with oak shaded streets, a historic spa and a Main Street full of local shops.
day: You walk the waterfront park and pier, then have dinner on Main Street without moving the car.
watch: Bayfront storm surge

pick_todo.name: Main Street
pick_todo.note: Local restaurants and shops, with a street festival on the third Friday of the month.

pick_meet.name: Third Friday
pick_meet.note: A monthly street celebration with music and food along Main Street.

pick_meet.name: Market on Main
pick_meet.note: The weekly Sunday farmers market.

pick_meet.name: Safety Harbor Art and Music Center
pick_meet.note: Concerts, art classes, open studios and a Tuesday writing workshop.

pick_meet.name: Pints of Science
pick_meet.note: A talk night at the Art and Music Center. October 22 and November 19 in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Safety Harbor Museum and Cultural Center
pick_meet.note: Classes, workshops and local history.

name: St. Pete Beach
blurb: A wide Gulf beach anchored by the pink Don CeSar hotel, with the old fishing village of Pass-a-Grille at its tip.
day: You have breakfast in Pass-a-Grille, spend the day on the wide Gulf beach and stay for the sunset.
airport: Tampa (TPA) or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 35 minutes
watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024

pick_todo.name: Pass-a-Grille
pick_todo.note: A historic beach village with a sunset bell and no high rises.

pick_meet.name: Corey Avenue Sunday Market
pick_meet.note: Vendors and local produce every Sunday, year round.

pick_meet.name: Sip and Stroll
pick_meet.note: Drinks and live music on Corey Avenue the last Friday of the month, 5 to 8pm.

pick_meet.name: Suntan Art Center
pick_meet.note: A volunteer run arts group with classes, member shows and weekend Art on the Patio in Pass-a-Grille.

pick_meet.name: Corey Avenue street parties
pick_meet.note: Mardi Gras and St. Patrick's Day take over the avenue each year.

name: St. Petersburg
blurb: A sunny waterfront city with a walkable downtown, the Dalí Museum, murals on every block and Gulf beaches 20 minutes away.
day: You walk the waterfront parks to the Pier, wander the Saturday Morning Market and pick a brewery for the afternoon.
airport: Tampa (TPA), about 25 to 35 minutes, or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE)
watch: Flooding in low lying neighborhoods, rising prices

pick_todo.name: The Dalí Museum
pick_todo.note: A world class collection on the downtown waterfront.

pick_meet.name: Saturday Morning Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays from 9am to 2pm. At the Al Lang Stadium lot from October through May and at Williams Park in summer.

pick_meet.name: Second Saturday ArtWalk
pick_meet.note: Galleries and studios in five arts districts open from 5 to 9pm on the second Saturday of every month.

pick_meet.name: St. Petersburg Shuffleboard Club
pick_meet.note: Open play on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and Sunday mornings, plus the Friday night shuffle from 7 to 10pm. Guests pay $10.

pick_meet.name: St. Pete Running Company run club
pick_meet.note: Group runs for runners and walkers of all paces. One of several run clubs in town.

pick_meet.name: Tampa Bay Club Sport
pick_meet.note: Adult leagues in kickball, volleyball, softball, soccer, pickleball and more around Tampa Bay, with 2026 seasons under way.

name: Sun City Center
blurb: A golf cart community inland from Tampa Bay with more than 100 clubs. Most homes here are age restricted to 55 and over.
day: You take the golf cart to a morning club meeting, play nine holes and drive it to dinner.
watch: Inland, so there is no beach. Most homes are age restricted to 55 and over

pick_todo.name: Community clubs
pick_todo.note: More than 100 clubs and activity groups, from woodworking to pickleball.

pick_meet.name: Community Association clubs
pick_meet.note: Well over 100 clubs, from ham radio and woodworking to photography and investing. Membership comes with living in the community.

pick_meet.name: Arts and crafts clubs
pick_meet.note: More than 20, including ceramics, stained glass, wood carving and model railroads.

pick_meet.name: Lawn bowling, pickleball and tennis
pick_meet.note: Thirteen outdoor clubs share the greens and courts.

pick_meet.name: Dance and music clubs
pick_meet.note: More than 15, from ballroom to line dancing.

pick_meet.name: Stage shows and the travel club
pick_meet.note: Regular shows at the community theater and organized group trips.

name: Tampa
blurb: The big city of the Gulf coast: a downtown riverwalk, historic Ybor City, pro sports and a major airport.
day: You run the Riverwalk before work, meet friends in Ybor City after and catch a Lightning game downtown.
watch: Flooding in low areas (Helene and Milton in 2024), traffic

pick_todo.name: Tampa Riverwalk
pick_todo.note: About 2.6 miles of waterfront path linking parks, museums and restaurants.

pick_meet.name: Ybor City Saturday Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday from 9am to 3pm in Centennial Park, all year.

pick_meet.name: Armature Works Run Club
pick_meet.note: A social run club based at the food hall on the Riverwalk in Tampa Heights.

pick_meet.name: Champs Run Club
pick_meet.note: A free 3K on the Riverwalk that starts and ends at Armature Works, held about four times a year.

pick_meet.name: Tampa Bay Club Sport
pick_meet.note: Adult leagues in kickball, volleyball, softball, soccer, flag football, pickleball and more, with 2026 seasons under way.

pick_meet.name: Gasparilla Pirate Fest
pick_meet.note: A mock pirate invasion and parade along Bayshore Boulevard each winter, first held in 1904.

name: Tarpon Springs
blurb: A working sponge port with Greek bakeries and restaurants along the docks and bayous winding through town.
day: You walk the Sponge Docks for coffee and pastry, watch the boats unload and drive to Fred Howard Park for the sunset.
watch: Flooding near the bayous and river. Helene's surge flooded the Sponge Docks in 2024

pick_todo.name: The Sponge Docks
pick_todo.note: Sponge boats, restaurants and bakeries along Dodecanese Boulevard.

pick_meet.name: Tarpon Arts volunteers
pick_meet.note: Help out at the Performing Arts Center, Cultural Center, Heritage Museum and Safford House.

pick_meet.name: Friends of Anclote Key
pick_meet.note: The volunteer group for the state park. It runs monthly lighthouse tours.

pick_meet.name: Tarpon Talks
pick_meet.note: A speaker series from Tarpon Arts. The November 10, 2026 talk covers Weedon Island Preserve.

pick_meet.name: Live music at Sunset Beach
pick_meet.note: Monthly concerts at the bandshell by the water.

pick_meet.name: Tarpon Springs Golf Course
pick_meet.note: The historic city course, part of the Florida Historic Golf Trail.

name: Treasure Island
blurb: A barrier island with one of the widest beaches on the Gulf.
day: You cross a long stretch of sand to reach the water, and on Sundays you stay for the drum circle at sunset.
airport: Tampa (TPA) or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 35 minutes
watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024

pick_todo.name: Treasure Island Beach Trail
pick_todo.note: A paved walkway about a mile long, running along the dunes.

pick_meet.name: Sunday drum circle
pick_meet.note: Drummers and dancers gather on the beach by the Gulf Front lot every Sunday until sunset.

pick_meet.name: Corey Avenue Sunday Market
pick_meet.note: One island south in St. Pete Beach, every Sunday year round.

pick_meet.name: Sanding Ovations
pick_meet.note: The sand sculpture festival each November. It came back in 2025 after a two year storm break.

pick_meet.name: Treasure Bay Golf, Tennis and Recreation Center
pick_meet.note: The city's rec hub, with golf, tennis and seasonal community events.

name: Bradenton
blurb: A river city with a long Riverwalk, spring training baseball and the Anna Maria Island beaches 20 minutes west.
day: You walk the Riverwalk in the morning, catch a Pirates spring training game and head to the island for sunset.
watch: Flooding along the river

pick_todo.name: Village of the Arts
pick_todo.note: A neighborhood of colorful cottages turned into galleries and cafes.

pick_meet.name: Bradenton Runners Club
pick_meet.note: Tuesday and Thursday at 6:30am from the Manatee Central Library, Saturday at 7am from the Bishop Museum and Sunday at 7am at Robinson Preserve.

pick_meet.name: Bradenton Public Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays from 9am to 2pm on Old Main Street, October through May.

pick_meet.name: Village of the Arts Art Walk
pick_meet.note: The first Friday and Saturday of each month, 11am to 4pm, in a neighborhood of studios and galleries founded in 1999.

pick_meet.name: Music in the Park
pick_meet.note: Free live music on the Riverwalk from Realize Bradenton. Dates for the coming season had not been announced.

pick_meet.name: Bradenton Arts and Music Festival
pick_meet.note: Several stages of live music plus live art on the Riverwalk, put on by Realize Bradenton.

name: Bradenton Beach
blurb: The south end of Anna Maria Island, with a historic fishing pier, a walkable Bridge Street and water on both sides.
day: You walk Bridge Street to the pier for breakfast and cross the road to the Gulf for the rest of the day.
watch: Island flooding. Hit hard by Helene in 2024. Cortez Bridge replacement work is planned through about 2029

pick_todo.name: Bridge Street
pick_todo.note: A short, walkable strip of restaurants and shops that ends at the pier.

pick_meet.name: Bradenton Runners Club
pick_meet.note: Saturday at 8am at Coquina Beach, a relaxed 2 to 4 miles.

pick_meet.name: Sundown Get Down
pick_meet.note: Street parties on Bridge Street from the Bridge Street Merchants Association. The October 2025 one was called Rock the Block.

pick_meet.name: Anna Maria Island Turtle Watch and Shorebird Monitoring
pick_meet.note: Volunteers patrol the island's beaches in nesting season, and the group holds a Turtle Watch Wednesday evening each fall.

pick_meet.name: The Center of Anna Maria Island
pick_meet.note: Adult soccer, flag football and 3v3 basketball leagues plus pickleball and tennis, up the island in Anna Maria.

pick_meet.name: Cortez Commercial Fishing Festival
pick_meet.note: Each February in the fishing village just across the bridge. 2026 was the 44th year.

name: Cortez
blurb: One of the last working fishing villages in Florida, with fish houses on the bay that date back to the 1880s.
day: You eat lunch at a fish house on the water and watch the boats come in.
watch: Low lying, with storm surge risk. The Cortez Bridge is set to be replaced, with work running to about 2029

pick_todo.name: Cortez Commercial Fishing Festival
pick_todo.note: A February weekend of seafood, music and boat tours.

pick_meet.name: Cortez Nautical Flea Market
pick_meet.note: Held on the grounds of the Florida Maritime Museum. The most recent was in March 2026.

pick_meet.name: Bradenton Runners Club
pick_meet.note: Saturday at 8am at Coquina Beach, about five minutes across the bridge.

pick_meet.name: Cortez Commercial Fishing Festival
pick_meet.note: Each February on the village waterfront, with seafood, live music and exhibits. 2026 was the 44th year.

pick_meet.name: Cortez Village Historical Society
pick_meet.note: Keeps the village history and hosts gatherings, including a Veterans Day tribute.

pick_meet.name: FISH Preserve
pick_meet.note: 98 acres of bayfront habitat held by a village nonprofit, with restoration under way after the 2024 hurricanes.

name: Englewood
blurb: A laid back Gulf town with a small old downtown and beaches on Manasota Key, known for shark teeth.
day: You walk Stump Pass Beach looking for shark teeth, then head to Dearborn Street for the farmers market.
watch: Storm surge. Hit by Ian in 2022 and by Helene and Milton in 2024

pick_todo.name: Stump Pass Beach State Park
pick_todo.note: A mile of undeveloped beach at the tip of Manasota Key.

pick_meet.name: The Market on Dearborn
pick_meet.note: Thursday farmers market on West Dearborn Street, 9am to 1pm, October through May.

pick_meet.name: Englewood Sailing Association
pick_meet.note: All volunteer nonprofit at Indian Mound Park. Adult learn to sail classes and a Wednesday social sail.

pick_meet.name: Lemon Bay Playhouse
pick_meet.note: Community theater on West Dearborn Street, now in its 39th season.

pick_meet.name: Stump Pass ranger hikes
pick_meet.note: Ranger led nature hikes at Stump Pass Beach State Park in the winter months.

pick_meet.name: Englewood Beach Waterfest
pick_meet.note: Offshore powerboat races off Englewood Beach each November.

name: Sarasota
blurb: The arts capital of the Gulf coast, with an opera, a ballet, The Ringling museum, Lido Beach just over the bridge and Siesta Key's famous sand minutes away.
day: You walk the bayfront at sunrise, spend the afternoon at The Ringling and see a show downtown at night.
watch: Storm surge (Helene and Milton in 2024), season traffic

pick_todo.name: The Ringling
pick_todo.note: An art museum, a circus museum and a bayfront mansion on 66 acres.

pick_todo.name: St. Armands Circle
pick_todo.note: A walkable circle of shops and restaurants on Lido Key, a few blocks from Lido Beach.

pick_meet.name: Sarasota Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday, 7am to 1pm, at Lemon Avenue and Main Street. Year round since 1979.

pick_meet.name: 99 Bottles Run Club
pick_meet.note: A 5K from the taproom through downtown and along the bayfront every Wednesday at 6pm. All paces, 150 to 250 runners a week.

pick_meet.name: The Bay
pick_meet.note: Free fitness classes and events all year at the bayfront park on Boulevard of the Arts.

pick_meet.name: Sarasota Sailing Squadron
pick_meet.note: Nonprofit community sailing club on City Island with adult lessons, regattas and open membership.

pick_meet.name: Friends of the Legacy Trail
pick_meet.note: Volunteer group that looks after the trail and hosts socials like Taco Tuesdays, October through March.

pick_meet.name: Fitness in the Circle park
pick_meet.note: Yoga, pilates and Zumba classes in the park at the center of St. Armands Circle, with 2026 dates posted.

name: Siesta Key
blurb: An island of quartz white sand so fine it stays cool underfoot, with a small, lively village at the north end.
day: You walk to Siesta Beach before the crowds, have lunch in the Village and come back for the Sunday drum circle.
watch: Bridge traffic, storm surge

pick_todo.name: Siesta Beach
pick_todo.note: Named the number one beach in America by Tripadvisor in 2025.

pick_meet.name: Siesta Key Drum Circle
pick_meet.note: Sunday evenings on Siesta Beach, starting about an hour before sunset. Going since 1996.

pick_meet.name: Siesta Beach courts
pick_meet.note: Public pickleball and beach volleyball courts beside the sand.

pick_meet.name: Siesta Key Crystal Classic
pick_meet.note: Four days of master sand sculpting on Siesta Beach, November 13 to 16, 2026. This is its 17th year.

pick_meet.name: Siesta Key Holiday Parade
pick_meet.note: Chamber parade on November 28, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Scarecrow Stroll
pick_meet.note: Businesses put up handmade scarecrows on their storefronts through October.

name: Venice
blurb: A 1920s planned town of palm lined avenues you can walk from downtown to the Gulf, with newer mainland neighborhoods and the Legacy Trail just over the bridge.
day: You hunt for shark teeth on the beach, walk Venice Avenue for lunch and watch the sunset from the jetty.
watch: Storm surge on the island and near the water

pick_todo.name: Venice Avenue
pick_todo.note: A palm lined main street of shops and restaurants that ends at the beach.

pick_todo.name: The Legacy Trail
pick_todo.note: A paved rail trail of about 18 miles running north to Sarasota.

pick_meet.name: Venice Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday, 8am to 1pm, next to City Hall on West Venice Avenue. Year round, with more than 100 vendors.

pick_meet.name: Friday Night Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Free shows at the Centennial Park gazebo on the second and fourth Fridays, 7 to 9pm.

pick_meet.name: Venice Theatre
pick_meet.note: Community theater downtown with a season that runs July through June, plus workshops.

pick_meet.name: Beach yoga at Venice Beach
pick_meet.note: Morning and sunset sessions on the sand at the end of Venice Avenue.

pick_meet.name: Downtown Venice Art Festival
pick_meet.note: Two days on West Venice Avenue, October 31 and November 1, 2026. This is its 38th year.

pick_meet.name: Friends of the Legacy Trail
pick_meet.note: Volunteers who look after the trail. Taco Tuesday socials are the second Tuesday of the month, October through March, at Nokomis Community Park.

name: Bonita Springs
blurb: A city between Naples and Fort Myers with a small historic downtown, golf communities and a quiet Gulf beach on Little Hickory Island, next to Lovers Key.
day: You play a morning round, have lunch downtown by the river and catch the sunset at Bonita Beach.
watch: Season traffic on US 41, flood zones west of 41, storm surge at the beach. County beach parking lots were closed for repairs in fall 2026

pick_todo.name: Riverside Park
pick_todo.note: A downtown park on the Imperial River with concerts and art festivals.

pick_todo.name: Lovers Key State Park
pick_todo.note: Two miles of beach, plus trails and kayak routes through the mangroves.

pick_meet.name: Local Roots market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays from 8am to noon at Promenade at Bonita Bay, October 3, 2026 through May 29, 2027.

pick_meet.name: Arts Bonita
pick_meet.note: Classes, workshops and theater at the Visual Arts Center on Old 41 and the Performing Arts Center on Bonita Beach Road.

pick_meet.name: Bonita Springs Concert Band
pick_meet.note: Concerts at Riverside Park on December 13, 2026, then monthly from January through April 2027.

pick_meet.name: Everglades Wonder Gardens
pick_meet.note: The garden on Old 41 takes volunteers to help with its grounds and its rescued birds and reptiles.

pick_meet.name: Bonita Springs Parks and Recreation
pick_meet.note: Pickleball, fitness classes and lap swim at the city rec center, courts and community pool.

pick_meet.name: Lovers Key State Park volunteers
pick_meet.note: The park takes volunteers through the Florida State Parks program.

name: Cape Coral
blurb: A city of more than 400 miles of canals, where a boat in the back yard is normal and waterfront is still within reach.
day: You lower the boat off the lift, idle out the canal to the river and are fishing the Gulf within the hour.
watch: Storm surge (Ian in 2022) and insurance costs. Not every canal reaches the Gulf

pick_todo.name: Cape Harbour
pick_todo.note: A marina village with waterfront dining, live music and boat watching.

pick_meet.name: Cape Coral Farmers' Market
pick_meet.note: Saturday mornings at Club Square, SE 47th Terrace and SE 10th Place in South Cape.

pick_meet.name: Cape Bike Night
pick_meet.note: SE 47th Terrace closes for motorcycles, live music and food trucks a few evenings a year.

pick_meet.name: Cape Coral Art Center
pick_meet.note: City run classes, studios and exhibits.

pick_meet.name: Red, White & BOOM
pick_meet.note: The city's big July 4 street party and fireworks, held every year.

pick_meet.name: Island Hopper Songwriter Fest
pick_meet.note: Songwriter shows around town each September, shared with Captiva, Fort Myers and Fort Myers Beach.

name: Chokoloskee
blurb: A tiny shell mound island at the edge of Everglades National Park, the last stop before the Ten Thousand Islands.
day: You pole a skiff through the mangrove islands for snook and stop at the old Smallwood Store on the way in.
watch: Very low lying and isolated, with storm surge risk
season: Quiet. Winter is prime fishing season

pick_todo.name: Ten Thousand Islands
pick_todo.note: A maze of mangrove islands for fishing, paddling and camping.

pick_meet.name: Museum of the Everglades
pick_meet.note: Collier County's history museum in Everglades City, open Tuesday through Saturday.

pick_meet.name: Smallwood Store
pick_meet.note: The old trading post turned museum at the south end of the island.

pick_meet.name: Everglades Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: The 57th annual festival runs February 19 to 21, 2027 in Everglades City, with seafood, live country music and crafts.

pick_meet.name: Everglades National Park
pick_meet.note: The Gulf Coast area in Everglades City has boat tours and canoe and kayak rentals, and the park takes volunteers.

name: Everglades City
blurb: A small fishing town on the Barron River at the edge of Everglades National Park, known for stone crab and as the way into the Ten Thousand Islands.
day: You launch a kayak at the national park visitor center, eat stone crab on the river for lunch and catch the Third Thursday talk at the museum.
watch: Storm surge. Wilma in 2005, Irma in 2017 and Ian in 2022 all flooded town, and nearly every property is in a flood zone
season: Busy November through April, very quiet in summer

pick_todo.name: Everglades National Park, Gulf Coast
pick_todo.note: The new Marjory Stoneman Douglas Visitor Center opened in December 2025, with boat tours and a kayak launch.

pick_todo.name: Museum of the Everglades
pick_todo.note: The county's history museum, a short walk from the circle. Open Tuesday through Saturday.

pick_todo.name: Ten Thousand Islands
pick_todo.note: A maze of mangrove islands for fishing, paddling and camping, starting right off the dock.

pick_meet.name: Fresh Market
pick_meet.note: Fridays and Sundays from 10 to 2, beside the post office on Collier Avenue.

pick_meet.name: First Friday at the Rod and Gun Club
pick_meet.note: A social from 5 to 7pm on the first Friday of the month.

pick_meet.name: Museum of the Everglades talks
pick_meet.note: Free lectures on the third Thursday of the month, and a Friends group that takes volunteers.

pick_meet.name: Everglades Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: The 57th festival runs February 19 to 21, 2027 at City Hall.

pick_meet.name: Blessing of the Stone Crab Fleet
pick_meet.note: Early October, just before the season opens on October 15.

name: Fort Myers
blurb: The City of Palms, with a brick street River District downtown and the winter homes of Edison and Ford on the river.
day: You tour the Edison and Ford estates, walk First Street for dinner and catch live music in the River District.
watch: Flooding along the river. Hit by Ian in 2022

pick_todo.name: River District
pick_todo.note: Brick streets, restaurants and monthly art and music walks downtown.

pick_meet.name: Art Walk
pick_meet.note: The first Friday evening of every month, with galleries open across the River District.

pick_meet.name: Music Walk
pick_meet.note: The third Friday evening of every month, with live music on the streets and in the bars downtown.

pick_meet.name: Fort Myers Track Club
pick_meet.note: A long running club that puts on road races through the year.

pick_meet.name: Edison and Ford Winter Estates
pick_meet.note: Open daily, with a volunteer program, garden talks and classes on 20 acres by the river.

pick_meet.name: Sidney & Berne Davis Art Center
pick_meet.note: Classes, exhibitions and a live music series in the old federal building on First Street.

name: Fort Myers Beach
blurb: Seven miles of soft sand on Estero Island, rebuilding after Hurricane Ian with its beach town spirit intact.
day: You walk the beach at low tide, have lunch near Times Square and watch the shrimp boats head out at dusk.
watch: Still rebuilding after Hurricane Ian in 2022. Check flood zones and construction nearby

pick_meet.name: Bayside Park Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Outdoor concerts by the bay, steps from Times Square.

pick_meet.name: Mound House
pick_meet.note: Museum, guided kayak tours on Estero Bay and a volunteer program, on a 2,000 year old shell mound.

pick_meet.name: Fort Myers Beach Lions Club Shrimp Festival
pick_meet.note: Parade and vendors on Old San Carlos Boulevard each March. The 69th is March 13 and 14, 2027.

pick_meet.name: American Sand Sculpting Championship
pick_meet.note: Five days of pro sand sculpting each November. The 36th is November 19 to 23, 2026.

name: Marco Island
blurb: The largest of the Ten Thousand Islands, with a wide crescent beach on one side and wild mangrove country on the other.
day: You shell on Tigertail Beach at low tide, then take the boat into the Ten Thousand Islands for the afternoon.
watch: Storm surge, high insurance

pick_todo.name: Tigertail Beach
pick_todo.note: A lagoon and sandbar beach known for shelling and shorebirds.

pick_meet.name: Marco Island Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: A weekly city run market in the winter season. Check the city site for this season's dates and location.

pick_meet.name: Marco Island Center for the Arts
pick_meet.note: Classes, gallery receptions and a Lunch and Learn series.

pick_meet.name: Arts Center Theatre
pick_meet.note: Mainstage plays and a comedy series at Marco Town Center.

pick_meet.name: Friends of Rookery Bay
pick_meet.note: Volunteers help with conservation work across the estuary reserve.

pick_meet.name: Rookery Bay kayak tours
pick_meet.note: Guided paddles and kayak rentals in the mangrove reserve that surrounds the island.

name: Port Charlotte
blurb: A canal community on Charlotte Harbor with some of the most affordable waterfront homes in Southwest Florida.
day: You run the canals out to the harbor for tarpon and snook, then catch a spring training game at the ballpark.
watch: Storm damage history (Charley in 2004, Ian in 2022), flood zones

pick_todo.name: Charlotte Harbor
pick_todo.note: One of the best tarpon and snook fisheries in the state.

pick_meet.name: Port Charlotte Beach Park
pick_meet.note: County park on the harbor with a rec center, heated pool, and tennis, bocce and sand volleyball courts.

pick_meet.name: Rays spring training
pick_meet.note: Tampa Bay Rays games at Charlotte Sports Park, a 7,500 seat ballpark on El Jobean Road.

pick_meet.name: Tippecanoe Environmental Park
pick_meet.note: Trails, a boardwalk and a kayak launch next to the ballpark, with good birding.

pick_meet.name: Charlotte County Fair
pick_meet.note: Held at the fairgrounds in Port Charlotte, which also hosts festivals and boat shows through the year.

name: Punta Gorda
blurb: A small harbor town with brick streets, a waterfront Harborwalk and sailboat canals that lead to the Gulf.
day: You bike the Harborwalk, have lunch at Fishermen's Village and sail the harbor before sunset.
watch: Storm surge. Hit by Ian in 2022, and downtown flooded again in 2024

pick_todo.name: Harborwalk
pick_todo.note: A waterfront path linking parks, the marina and Fishermen's Village.

pick_meet.name: Punta Gorda Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Downtown market with produce, crafts and prepared food.

pick_meet.name: TEAM Punta Gorda
pick_meet.note: Volunteer group started after Hurricane Charley in 2004. Community projects, mixers and a bicycle loaner program.

pick_meet.name: PicklePlex
pick_meet.note: Pickleball complex built with community donations and run by a nonprofit board.

pick_meet.name: Visual Arts Center
pick_meet.note: A 12,000 square foot center with galleries, studios and classes for all skill levels.

pick_meet.name: Mural walking tours
pick_meet.note: Guided walks past 31 murals of local history, a project that dates to 1995.

name: Sanibel Island
blurb: A barrier island famous for shells, with 25 miles of bike paths, no traffic lights and more than half the island preserved.
day: You do the Sanibel stoop for shells at sunrise, bike to the Ding Darling refuge and ride home for the sunset.
watch: Hit hard by Hurricane Ian in 2022 and mostly rebuilt. Check flood zones. The causeway is the only road

pick_todo.name: J.N. Ding Darling National Wildlife Refuge
pick_todo.note: Thousands of acres of mangroves and wading birds.

pick_meet.name: Sanibel Island Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Sunday mornings at City Hall on Dunlop Road in season, which ran through May in 2026.

pick_meet.name: BIG ARTS
pick_meet.note: Classes and workshops, Monday Night Cinema, gallery shows and a concert season.

pick_meet.name: SCCF Coastal Watch
pick_meet.note: Volunteer beach cleanups, mangrove and oyster restoration, and sea turtle and shorebird monitoring.

pick_meet.name: Sanibel Bicycle Club
pick_meet.note: Group rides on the shared use paths and through the Ding Darling refuge.

pick_meet.name: Sanibel Shell Show and Festival
pick_meet.note: Three days each March at The Community House. 2026 was the 89th.

name: Key Largo
blurb: The first Key off the mainland and the dive capital of the country, with a coral reef state park offshore.
day: You're on a dive boat to the reef by 8, back for fish tacos by the water at noon and in a hammock by 2.
watch: A long evacuation drive, high insurance

pick_todo.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
pick_todo.note: The first undersea park in the country, for snorkeling, diving and glass bottom boats.

pick_meet.name: REEF
pick_meet.note: Based in Key Largo. Volunteer fish surveys for divers and snorkelers, a monthly Fish and Friends seminar and REEF Fest each October.

pick_meet.name: Coral Restoration Foundation
pick_meet.note: Hands on dive and snorkel programs from its Exploration Center on Seagate Boulevard, plus events like full moon yoga.

pick_meet.name: Upper Keys Sailing Club
pick_meet.note: A sailing club on Ocean Bay Drive, on the bay side of Key Largo.

pick_meet.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
pick_meet.note: Snorkel, dive and glass bottom boats every day, plus kayak and paddleboard rentals.

pick_meet.name: Dagny Johnson Key Largo Hammock Botanical State Park
pick_meet.note: Ranger guided walks and more than six miles of trails for walking and biking.

name: Bal Harbour
blurb: A tiny oceanfront village at the north tip of Miami Beach, known for a luxury shopping center and a quiet beach path.
day: You jog the beach path at sunrise, have a long lunch at the Bal Harbour Shops and walk the beach at dusk.
airport: Miami (MIA) or Fort Lauderdale (FLL), about 35 minutes
watch: Very high prices, flooding, traffic

pick_todo.name: Bal Harbour Shops
pick_todo.note: An open air luxury mall with palm lined courtyards.

pick_meet.name: The Market at Bal Harbour
pick_meet.note: The village market, Saturdays and Sundays from 10am to 4pm.

pick_meet.name: Sounds by the Sea
pick_meet.note: A monthly oceanfront concert series put on by the village.

pick_meet.name: Movie Night on the Beach
pick_meet.note: Outdoor film nights on the village events calendar.

pick_meet.name: Waterfront Park community center
pick_meet.note: Classes and programs through the village recreation department, plus fitness stations and a basketball court.

pick_meet.name: Haulover Park
pick_meet.note: Just across the inlet, with a kite field, pump track, dog park and food trucks on Tuesday evenings.

name: Boca Raton
blurb: A polished city of pink Mediterranean buildings, big parks and beaches kept natural behind a line of dunes.
day: You walk the boardwalk at Gumbo Limbo, have lunch at Mizner Park and catch an outdoor concert at the amphitheater.
airport: Palm Beach airport or Fort Lauderdale (FLL), about 30 minutes
watch: Traffic, higher insurance

pick_todo.name: Mizner Park
pick_todo.note: A walkable plaza of shops, restaurants, an art museum and an amphitheater.

pick_meet.name: City community events
pick_meet.note: Boca Street Fest, the Night Market, Battle of the Bands and Summer in the City fill the calendar through the year.

pick_meet.name: The Racquet Center
pick_meet.note: 26 clay courts with clinics, leagues, a challenge ladder and a Looking for a Game program that pairs you with players.

pick_meet.name: Boca Raton Museum of Art
pick_meet.note: Lecture series, gallery tours and a film series at Mizner Park, plus classes at its Art School on Palmetto Park Road.

pick_meet.name: Sugar Sand Park Field House
pick_meet.note: Home base for the city's adult classes and leagues, open into the evening most nights.

pick_meet.name: Festival of the Arts BOCA
pick_meet.note: Ten days of concerts and talks each March. Season 21 runs March 5 to 14, 2027.

name: Dania Beach
blurb: A small, unflashy beach city right next to the Fort Lauderdale airport, with a fishing pier and a quiet beach.
day: You fish off the pier at sunrise, have lunch at a dockside spot and can be at your gate 15 minutes after leaving home.
watch: Airport noise, flooding

pick_todo.name: Dania Beach Pier
pick_todo.note: A long fishing pier with a restaurant at the foot.

pick_meet.name: Dania Pointe seasonal events
pick_meet.note: A Fall Artisan Market with live music, a 5K fun run in October and a Food and Wine Festival in November.

pick_meet.name: Wellness Wednesdays at Dania Pointe
pick_meet.note: Yoga at 6pm and Zumba at 7pm every Wednesday on The Lawn.

pick_meet.name: Whiskey Creek Hideout
pick_meet.note: Kayak and paddleboard rentals and guided paddles inside Mizell-Eula Johnson State Park.

pick_meet.name: Dania Beach Fishing Pier
pick_meet.note: A 974 foot pier with a bait shop, lit for night fishing, where the regulars line the rail at sunrise.

pick_meet.name: The Casino at Dania Beach
pick_meet.note: Live jai alai, plus tribute concerts and comedy nights on the calendar through fall 2026.

name: Hallandale Beach
blurb: A city of oceanfront condo towers between Fort Lauderdale and Miami, home to Gulfstream Park.
day: You walk the beach in the morning, watch the horses run at Gulfstream Park and stay for dinner in the village there.
watch: Traffic, flooding, condo fees and assessments

pick_todo.name: Gulfstream Park
pick_todo.note: Horse racing, a casino and an outdoor village of shops and restaurants.

pick_meet.name: Live racing at Gulfstream Park
pick_meet.note: Friday through Sunday during the fall 2026 Sunshine Meet, with more race days in the winter Championship Meet.

pick_meet.name: Yellow Green Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Ten minutes north in Hollywood. Saturdays and Sundays, 10am to 6:30pm, year round.

pick_meet.name: Pegasus World Cup
pick_meet.note: The track's biggest day, held each January. 2026 was its tenth year.

pick_meet.name: Florida Derby
pick_meet.note: The spring stakes day at Gulfstream Park and one of its busiest afternoons.

name: Highland Beach
blurb: A three mile strip of oceanfront condos and homes between Boca Raton and Delray Beach, with no shops and no crowds.
day: You walk a beach with almost nobody on it, then drive ten minutes to Atlantic Avenue when you want company.
watch: Oceanfront storm exposure, high condo fees

pick_meet.name: Happy hour at Latitudes
pick_meet.note: Monday through Friday from 4 to 6pm at the Delray Sands Resort, the one gathering spot on the ocean.

pick_meet.name: Delray Beach Winter GreenMarket
pick_meet.note: About 10 minutes north. Saturdays at Old School Square from late October through May.

pick_meet.name: Delray Beach First Friday Art Walk
pick_meet.note: Galleries stay open late the first Friday of every month, 6 to 9pm.

pick_meet.name: Highland Beach Library
pick_meet.note: The town library on South Ocean Boulevard, and the usual home for talks, classes and art exhibits in town.

pick_meet.name: Gumbo Limbo Nature Center
pick_meet.note: A few minutes south in Boca Raton, with a boardwalk, a 40 foot observation tower and outdoor marine aquariums.

name: Hollywood
blurb: A beach city with a 2.5 mile oceanfront Broadwalk for walking and biking, plus a downtown full of murals.
day: You bike the Broadwalk before it gets hot, stop for breakfast a few steps from the sand and catch a concert at the bandshell.
watch: Flooding in low areas, traffic

pick_todo.name: Hollywood Beach Broadwalk
pick_todo.note: A 2.5 mile brick promenade along the ocean, lined with cafes.

pick_meet.name: Hollywood Beach Theatre
pick_meet.note: Free live music with space for dancing on the Broadwalk at Johnson Street, Thursday through Sunday, 7 to 9pm.

pick_meet.name: Yellow Green Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays and Sundays, 10am to 6:30pm, year round on Sheridan Street.

pick_meet.name: ArtsPark at Young Circle
pick_meet.note: Free movie nights, concerts and weekend festivals in the downtown park.

pick_meet.name: Beach Sweep
pick_meet.note: Volunteer beach cleanup mornings. The October 2026 sweep ran from 7 to 11am.

pick_meet.name: Hollywood Beach Half Marathon & 5K
pick_meet.note: An October race on the beach and Broadwalk. The 2026 date is October 17.

name: Lauderdale by the Sea
blurb: A low rise beach village where a coral reef sits close enough to shore that you can snorkel it from the sand.
day: You snorkel the reef off the beach in the morning, walk to lunch in the square and listen to live music there at night.
watch: Oceanfront storm exposure

pick_todo.name: Anglin's Square
pick_todo.note: The little downtown by the pier, with restaurants and outdoor music.

pick_meet.name: Farmers' Market at El Prado Park
pick_meet.note: Sundays from 9am to 1pm, December 6, 2026 through May 2, 2027.

pick_meet.name: Friday Night Music
pick_meet.note: The town's seasonal outdoor concert series. Dates for the 2027 series had not been posted as of October 2026.

pick_meet.name: BugFest-By-The-Sea
pick_meet.note: A two day lobster season festival each July, with dive contests, seminars and concerts.

pick_meet.name: Community Center at Jarvis Hall
pick_meet.note: Monthly events and classes at 4505 Ocean Drive.

pick_meet.name: Fourth of July Parade
pick_meet.note: One of the oldest in Broward County, held since 1960, with fireworks off El Prado Park.

name: Lighthouse Point
