pick_meet.note: City courts on South Palmetto Avenue, across from the riverfront park.

pick_meet.name: Piggotte Community Center
pick_meet.note: The city's community center on Big Tree Road, used for city programs and private events.

pick_meet.name: Reed Canal Park
pick_meet.note: A city park with rentable pavilions for get togethers.

pick_meet.name: Riverwalk Social
pick_meet.note: A food truck court with live music on the river in Port Orange, a few minutes south.

pick_meet.name: Halifax Art Festival
pick_meet.note: An art festival in Daytona's Riverfront Arts District each November.

name: Navarre
blurb: The mainland side of Navarre, a growing stretch of neighborhoods along Santa Rosa Sound with Navarre Beach a short causeway drive away.
day: You launch a kayak into the sound in the morning, run errands along Highway 98, and drive five minutes over the causeway for an evening swim on Navarre Beach.
airport: Pensacola (PNS) about 45 minutes, Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS) about 45 to 60
watch: Highway 98 congestion at rush hour, hurricane and surge exposure along the sound, few road alternatives
season: Busy summer traffic on Highway 98, calm in winter

pick_todo.name: Navarre Park
pick_todo.note: The town's sound front park on Highway 98, with a splash pad, playground, pavilions and the Black Hawk Memorial.

pick_meet.name: Saturday market
pick_meet.note: A seasonal Saturday morning market with local growers and makers, a good place to see neighbors.

pick_meet.name: Navarre Park
pick_meet.note: The sound front park on Highway 98 with a splash pad, pavilions and the Black Hawk Memorial, where a lot of community events happen.

pick_meet.name: Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center
pick_meet.note: Volunteer run and open year round on the island, a natural way to meet people who love the beach.

pick_meet.name: Sound side boat ramps
pick_meet.note: Early mornings at the ramps are where anglers and paddlers swap reports.

name: Mary Esther
blurb: A small, settled city on Santa Rosa Sound between Fort Walton Beach and Hurlburt Field, with sound front streets and some of the most approachable prices in the area.
day: You fish off the little city pier on the sound in the morning, grab lunch in Fort Walton Beach and drive over the bridge to Okaloosa Island for a late swim.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 30 minutes
watch: Highway 98 traffic, aircraft noise near Hurlburt Field, storm surge on the sound side
season: Steady year round, Highway 98 busier in summer

pick_todo.name: Mary Esther city pier and boat ramp
pick_todo.note: A small public pier and ramp on Santa Rosa Sound off Misty Water Lane, handy for a quick launch or sunset fishing.

pick_meet.name: Concerts at the Landing
pick_meet.note: Free Friday night shows on the water in downtown Fort Walton Beach, a few minutes east, that draw people from all over the area.

pick_meet.name: Mary Esther city pier
pick_meet.note: The small pier and ramp on the sound where locals fish, launch kayaks and watch the sunset.

pick_meet.name: Santa Rosa Mall area
pick_meet.note: The theater, Surge Adventure Park and gym stayed open while the old mall is redeveloped into a mixed use center.

name: Fort Walton Beach
blurb: An unpretentious waterfront city on Santa Rosa Sound with a walkable old downtown, a calendar full of local events and Okaloosa Island's beaches just over the bridge.
day: You get coffee downtown, walk the sound front at the Landing, spend the afternoon on Okaloosa Island and come back for a free Friday concert by the water.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 20 minutes
watch: Brooks Bridge construction until about 2029, Highway 98 traffic, storm surge along the sound and bayous
season: Busy summers, lively spring festival season

pick_todo.name: Fort Walton Beach Landing
pick_todo.note: The renovated downtown park on the sound that hosts free Friday concerts in spring and the Fourth of July fireworks.

pick_meet.name: Concerts at the Landing
pick_meet.note: Free Friday night shows from 6 to 8 at the Landing on the sound. The 2026 spring series ran May 8 through June 5.

pick_meet.name: Billy Bowlegs Pirate Festival
pick_meet.note: The city's signature festival each May, with a pirate landing, treasure hunts and a torchlight parade down Eglin Parkway. 2026 was its 70th year.

pick_meet.name: Heritage Park and Cultural Center
pick_meet.note: Downtown museums around a temple mound, with exhibits on local history from prehistoric times to the 1950s.

pick_meet.name: Fourth of July at the Landing
pick_meet.note: Live music and fireworks over Santa Rosa Sound, one of the biggest nights of the year downtown.

name: Okaloosa Island
blurb: A short barrier island strip across the bridge from Fort Walton Beach, with a Gulf pier, a beachfront boardwalk, the Gulfarium and undeveloped land running east toward Destin.
day: You fish the pier at sunrise, spend the day on the white sand, and end with live music and a sunset on the Boardwalk.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 20 to 25 minutes
watch: Barrier island hurricane exposure, Brooks Bridge construction, summer crowds, check land lease and condo association details
season: Very busy March through summer, quiet in winter

pick_todo.name: The Island Pier
pick_todo.note: A 1,262 foot Gulf pier with a tackle shop and grill, open around the clock from April through October.

pick_meet.name: The Island Pier
pick_meet.note: Fishing and walking all day, open 24 hours April through October. The tackle shop and grill keep it social.

pick_meet.name: The Boardwalk on Okaloosa Island
pick_meet.note: Restaurants and bars next to the pier, with nightly live music at Al's Beach Club in season and free New Year's Eve fireworks.

pick_meet.name: Gulfarium Marine Adventure Park
pick_meet.note: The 70 year old marine park on the island, with memberships, member events and a sea turtle rescue center.

pick_meet.name: Okaloosa Island Boat Basin
pick_meet.note: The rebuilt county facility on the sound with a kayak launch, fishing pier and slips.

name: Shalimar
blurb: A tiny, leafy town on Choctawhatchee Bay and its bayous, just north of Fort Walton Beach, with shady streets, docks and a waterfront golf course.
day: You take the boat out of the bayou in the morning, play a round by the bay in the afternoon and are home in time to watch the sunset off the dock.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 10 to 15 minutes
watch: Eglin Parkway traffic, jet noise from Eglin, storm surge on low bayfront lots

pick_todo.name: Shalimar Pointe Golf Club
pick_todo.note: An 18 hole course on Choctawhatchee Bay with year round tee times.

pick_meet.name: Shalimar Pointe Golf Club
pick_meet.note: The bayfront course where a lot of locals play and gather.

pick_meet.name: Meigs Park and boat ramp
pick_meet.note: The county ramp and park on the bay where boaters and anglers cross paths.

pick_meet.name: Longwood Poquito Bayou Park
pick_meet.note: A small county park and ramp on Poquito Bayou, good for a paddle or an evening walk.

pick_meet.name: Shalimar Library
pick_meet.note: The volunteer run town library, a low key way to get involved.

name: Niceville
blurb: A bayside town on Choctawhatchee Bay where boats tie up on the bayous and the Gulf beaches are a short drive away.
day: You paddle Turkey Creek in the morning, grab grouper by the water at lunch and watch the sunset over Boggy Bayou from Niceville Landing.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 15 minutes
watch: Bayou storm surge in low areas, Eglin jet noise, John Sims Parkway and Mid Bay Bridge traffic, Gulf beaches are a 30 minute drive
season: Steady all year, light tourist swing

pick_todo.name: Turkey Creek Park
pick_todo.note: A one mile boardwalk nature trail plus a clear, cool creek for tubing and paddling.

pick_meet.name: Niceville Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays 9 to 1 year round at the Twin Cities Pavilion on John Sims Parkway, with local produce, baked goods and crafts.

pick_meet.name: Turkey Creek Park
pick_meet.note: Boardwalk walks, tubing and paddling, an easy place to run into neighbors on weekends.

pick_meet.name: Mattie Kelly Arts Center
pick_meet.note: The performing arts center at Northwest Florida State College, now in its 30th season of music, theater and art.

pick_meet.name: Artful Things Niceville
pick_meet.note: A local gift and art shop that hosts monthly guided painting sessions.

name: Valparaiso
blurb: A small, older bayou town tucked between Eglin Air Force Base and Boggy Bayou, right next door to Niceville.
day: You launch the boat at Lincoln Park before breakfast, fish the bayou all morning and are back on the porch by the time the afternoon storms roll in.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 10 minutes
watch: Low lying bayou streets can flood in storms, Eglin jet noise, very little room to grow so few homes come up for sale, Gulf beaches are about 30 minutes away
season: Steady all year, little tourist swing

pick_todo.name: Lincoln Park
pick_todo.note: The city's main waterfront park on Boggy Bayou, with a 24 hour boat ramp, swimming area with docks and picnic spots.

pick_meet.name: Niceville Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Next door in Niceville on Saturday mornings, where a lot of Valparaiso shops too.

pick_meet.name: Lincoln Park
pick_meet.note: The town's gathering spot on Boggy Bayou, with the boat ramp, swimming docks and the annual Fourth of July celebration.

pick_meet.name: Heritage Museum of Northwest Florida
pick_meet.note: A small regional history museum in town that hosts community events through the year.

name: Miramar Beach
blurb: The stretch of Gulf front between Destin and 30A, with sugar white beaches, Sandestin's shops and a lot going on all year.
day: You catch the early beach before the lots fill, walk the Saturday market at Grand Boulevard and end the day with a sunset dinner on the sand.
airport: Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 30 minutes
watch: Heavy US 98 traffic in season, beach parking fills early, condo HOA and insurance costs, Gulf front hurricane exposure
season: Very busy summers and spring break

pick_todo.name: Miramar Beach Regional Access
pick_todo.note: The main public beach off Scenic Gulf Drive, with free parking and a long run of white sand.

pick_meet.name: Grand Boulevard Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays 9 to 1 year round at Grand Boulevard at Sandestin, with local farms, food and crafts.

pick_meet.name: Bands on the Boulevard
pick_meet.note: Free Thursday evening concerts on Grand Boulevard, May through early July in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Village of Baytowne Wharf
pick_meet.note: The village at Sandestin hosts a Mardi Gras parade, holiday events and summer concerts.

pick_meet.name: Miramar Park
pick_meet.note: Over 1,100 feet of public Gulf frontage with a snorkeling reef just offshore.

name: Freeport
blurb: A fast growing inland town on the bay side of Walton County, where newer neighborhoods sit a short drive from the 30A beaches.
day: You walk the trails at Hammock Bay in the morning, crab off LaGrange Bayou in the afternoon and drive down 331 for a sunset on the Gulf.
airport: Northwest Florida Beaches (ECP) or Destin Fort Walton Beach (VPS), about 45 minutes
watch: Fast growth and US 331 traffic, lots of new construction, Gulf beaches are 25 to 30 minutes away, low areas near the bayous can flood
season: Steady all year, beach traffic on US 331 in summer

pick_todo.name: Eden Gardens State Park
pick_todo.note: Old live oaks, gardens and the historic Wesley Mansion on Tucker Bayou, just south of town.

pick_meet.name: Freeport Bayfest
pick_meet.note: The city's fall festival at the regional sports complex in Hammock Bay, held each November.

pick_meet.name: Freeport Regional Sports Complex
pick_meet.note: Ballfields and new pickleball courts that draw a lot of local leagues and tournaments.

pick_meet.name: Eden Gardens State Park
pick_meet.note: Picnics, garden walks and a paddle launch on Tucker Bayou.

pick_meet.name: Fourth of July Parade and Fireworks
pick_meet.note: The city's summer celebration, a big turnout for a small town.

name: Mexico Beach
blurb: A small, quiet Gulf town on the Forgotten Coast that was nearly wiped out by Hurricane Michael and has steadily rebuilt around its wide, uncrowded beach.
day: You walk the squeaky white sand at sunrise, fish the canal or take the boat out to the reefs and finish with a fish taco on the beach.
watch: Took a direct hit from Hurricane Michael in 2018, still rebuilding; high wind and flood insurance; no lifeguards; pier rebuild will narrow traffic for about a year; few services in town

pick_todo.name: Sunset Park
pick_todo.note: The main public beach access, with parking, restrooms, showers and picnic pavilions.

pick_meet.name: Mexico Beach Gumbo Cookoff
pick_meet.note: A spring cookoff at the boat ramp, run by the volunteer special events team since 1999, that raises money for the July fireworks.

pick_meet.name: MBARA Kingfish Tournament
pick_meet.note: The reef association's July fishing tournament and captains party at the public boat ramp.

pick_meet.name: Fourth of July on the beach
pick_meet.note: A morning 5K and fireworks over the Gulf, a big night for the whole town.

pick_meet.name: Sunset Park
pick_meet.note: The main beach access, where locals gather for sunsets.

name: Keaton Beach
blurb: A small canal and fishing community on the Taylor County coast, where the boat ramp and the flats matter more than anything on land.
day: You launch at the county ramp at first light, spend the morning on the grass flats after trout or scallops, and are back on the porch by the canal when the afternoon storms roll in.
watch: Idalia (2023) and Helene (2024) both landed here and county leaders estimated 90% of homes were destroyed in Helene. Rebuilding is slow, many lots are empty or have campers, flood insurance and elevation rules drive the cost
season: Busiest in summer scallop season, very quiet the rest of the year

pick_todo.name: Keaton Beach public boat ramp
pick_todo.note: The county's main ramp, repaired with new docks in 2025, and the start of most days out on the flats.

pick_meet.name: Keaton Beach boat ramp
pick_meet.note: The everyday meeting spot, where fishing reports get traded every morning.

pick_meet.name: Summer scallop season
pick_meet.note: The busiest stretch of the year, when boats crowd the flats and the whole coast comes out.

pick_meet.name: Hodges Park
pick_meet.note: The county beach and pier park, being rebuilt after Helene, and the traditional gathering place on holidays.

pick_meet.name: Perry
pick_meet.note: The county seat about 30 minutes inland, with groceries, restaurants and most community events.

name: Horseshoe Beach
blurb: A tiny fishing town at the end of the road in Dixie County, built around canals, a little Main Street and open Gulf flats.
day: You run out to the flats in the morning for trout and scallops, spend the afternoon working on the dock, and catch up with neighbors on Main Street in the evening.
watch: Hit by Idalia (2023), Debby and Helene (2024). The mayor estimated about 175 of 365 homes were lost and every business closed after Helene. Rebuilding is slow, insurance is costly and the next storm is a real risk
season: Busiest in summer scallop and fishing season

pick_todo.name: Labor Day weekend in town
pick_todo.note: A parade, face painting and a themed night with live music at Sam's Plaza, held again in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Labor Day weekend celebration
pick_meet.note: Parade, face painting and a themed music night at Sam's Plaza, held again in September 2026.

pick_meet.name: Main Street
pick_meet.note: The small heart of town, where neighbors catch up and plan the next event.

pick_meet.name: Summer scallop season
pick_meet.note: The busiest weeks of the year, when the flats fill with boats and the canals come alive.

pick_meet.name: Horseshoe Beach park
pick_meet.note: The little waterfront park and beach in town, a natural gathering spot at sunset.

name: Suwannee
blurb: A canal town at the mouth of the Suwannee River, wrapped in a national wildlife refuge, where nearly every street ends at a dock.
day: You take the boat down the river past cypress and marsh to the Gulf, fish the creek mouths all morning, and stop at Salt Creek for a seafood lunch on the way home.
watch: Helene (2024) put about 12 feet of water into the marina and wrecked homes, docks and businesses. Many owners chose not to rebuild, and locals say the town could not take another storm like that without changes. One road in and out
season: Busiest in spring and summer fishing season, quiet in winter

pick_todo.name: Lower Suwannee National Wildlife Refuge
pick_todo.note: Over 53,000 acres of cypress swamp, salt marsh and pine around the river mouth, with trails and creeks to paddle.

pick_meet.name: Suwannee River
pick_meet.note: Weekend boat runs up to old landings like Fowler's Bluff, where river people gather.

pick_meet.name: Salt Creek Restaurant
pick_meet.note: The town's seafood spot, back open since February 2025 and the easiest place to meet locals.

pick_meet.name: Suwannee Marina
pick_meet.note: Boat rentals, bait and a river guide service, and the place to hear what is biting.

pick_meet.name: Lower Suwannee National Wildlife Refuge
pick_meet.note: Trails and paddling routes where you will run into other birders and kayakers.

name: Yankeetown
blurb: An old river town on the Withlacoochee a few miles from the Gulf, with live oaks, fish camps and a big nature preserve at the end of the road.
day: You launch a kayak at Bird Creek Park, paddle the marsh out toward the Gulf, and spend the afternoon watching birds from the tower at the Withlacoochee Gulf Preserve.
airport: Gainesville (GNV), about 1 hour 15 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 1 hour 45 minutes
watch: The whole town sits in the flood zone. Helene (2024) pushed a surge of about 12 feet into nearly all of Yankeetown and many homes flooded. Few owners carry flood insurance, so check flood history on any home
season: Quiet year round, busiest around the November seafood festival and in fishing season

pick_todo.name: Withlacoochee Gulf Preserve
pick_todo.note: A 413 acre preserve with an observation tower, boardwalk, trails and a kayak launch to the Gulf.

pick_meet.name: Yankeetown Seafood Festival
pick_meet.note: Free festival the weekend before Thanksgiving, set for November 21 and 22, 2026, with two music stages, run by the Lions Club.

pick_meet.name: Bird Creek Park
pick_meet.note: The kayak launch at the end of the road, where Elvis filmed a movie in 1961 and paddlers meet every weekend.

pick_meet.name: Withlacoochee Gulf Preserve
pick_meet.note: Trails, a tower and an education center where birders, paddlers and volunteers gather.

pick_meet.name: Yankeetown Marina
pick_meet.note: Boat launch, fishing guides and the place to swap fishing reports.

name: Inglis
blurb: A small river town where the Withlacoochee, Lake Rousseau and the old barge canal meet, a few miles in from the Gulf.
day: You put the boat in below the dam in the morning, run the river out toward the Gulf and finish with a fried fish basket at a tiki bar in Yankeetown.
airport: Gainesville (GNV), about 1 hour 15 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 1 hour 45 minutes
watch: Low ground along the river and toward Yankeetown took surge in Idalia (2023) and Helene (2024), long drives to big shopping and hospitals
season: Quiet most of the year, a little busier with anglers and paddlers in spring and fall

pick_todo.name: Inglis Dam and Island Recreation Area
pick_todo.note: Paved and dirt trails on Inglis Island, plus boat ramps on Lake Rousseau and the river below the dam.

pick_meet.name: Inglis Dam boat ramps
pick_meet.note: Anglers and boaters gather at the ramps above and below the dam, and conversation comes easy while you wait to launch.

pick_meet.name: Inglis Island trails
pick_meet.note: A paved loop and miles of dirt trails where walkers, cyclists and riders cross paths every morning.

pick_meet.name: Withlacoochee Gulf Preserve
pick_meet.note: The Yankeetown preserve has a boardwalk, an observation tower and paddling, and it draws birders and kayakers.

pick_meet.name: River and tiki bars in Yankeetown
pick_meet.note: Gator Cove and its neighbors are the casual meeting spots for locals and boaters.

name: Hernando Beach
blurb: A canal community on the Hernando County coast where most homes have a dock and a short run to the shallow Gulf flats.
day: You idle down the canal in the morning to fish the flats, take a swim at Pine Island in the afternoon and eat dinner on a patio by the water.
watch: Canal homes sit low and Helene (2024) pushed record surge into the community, insurance and elevation rules matter a lot
season: Busiest in scallop season and on summer weekends at Pine Island

pick_meet.name: Scallop season
pick_meet.note: Summer weekends on the flats feel like a floating neighborhood party.

pick_meet.name: Bayport Park
pick_meet.note: Pier, boat ramps and pavilions at the end of SR 50, busy with anglers at sunrise and sunset.

pick_meet.name: Alfred McKethan Pine Island Park
pick_meet.note: The local beach where people bring chairs, kids and dogs for the afternoon.

pick_meet.name: Rogers Park
pick_meet.note: A river beach and boat ramp on the Weeki Wachee where locals launch kayaks and cool off.

name: Weeki Wachee
blurb: A spring fed river corridor on the Nature Coast, best known for its mermaid shows and a clear blue river that runs a few miles to the Gulf.
day: You paddle the clear river in the morning, watch a mermaid show at noon and cool off at Rogers Park before dinner by the water.
watch: Riverfront homes near the coast sit in surge zones and Helene (2024) flooded low areas of western Hernando; paddle launch limits at the state park
season: Busy summer weekends at the springs and river, quieter in winter when manatees come in

pick_todo.name: Weeki Wachee Springs State Park
pick_todo.note: Mermaid shows, a summer waterpark and a guided kayak run down the spring fed river.

pick_meet.name: Rogers Park
pick_meet.note: A river beach, boat ramp and kayak rentals across the water, packed on warm weekends.

pick_meet.name: Spring Hill community groups
pick_meet.note: Clubs, leagues and markets in Spring Hill are where many residents build their social circle.

pick_meet.name: Weeki Wachee Springs State Park
pick_meet.note: Mermaid shows, the Buccaneer Bay waterpark in summer and the kayak launch keep this the area's main gathering spot.

pick_meet.name: Weeki Wachee Preserve
pick_meet.note: Trails and old shell roads where walkers, cyclists and birders run into each other.

name: Aripeka
blurb: A tiny old fishing village on Hammock Creek, straddling the Pasco and Hernando line, with stilt homes, marsh views and no stoplights.
day: You fish off the Hammock Creek bridge at sunrise, pick up stone crab claws in season and watch the sun drop over the marsh from your dock.
watch: Homes sit right on the creeks and marsh and many first floors flooded in Helene (2024), no restaurants or services in town
season: Quiet all year, a few more anglers and day trippers on spring and summer weekends

pick_todo.name: Hammock Creek bridge
pick_todo.note: A local favorite for fishing, with wide views of the marsh and the Gulf.

pick_meet.name: Hammock Creek bridge
pick_meet.note: Where locals and visitors fish, chat and watch the tide come in.

pick_meet.name: Aripeka Stone Crab Company
pick_meet.note: The family seafood shop by the bridge, a regular stop for neighbors.

pick_meet.name: Aripeka Sandhills Preserve
pick_meet.note: Trails through coastal hammock where walkers and birders cross paths.

pick_meet.name: Community clubhouse
pick_meet.note: The old village clubhouse is used for gatherings and meetings.

name: Hudson
blurb: A laid back Pasco County coast town with canal homes, a small beach strip of bars and seafood spots, and Tampa within an hour.
day: You take the boat out the Hudson channel in the morning, spend the afternoon at SunWest Park and end with a grouper sandwich and a sunset at Sam's.
airport: Tampa (TPA), about 50 minutes; St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 45 minutes
watch: Waterfront and canal homes flooded badly in Helene (2024), heavy traffic on US 19
season: Busier in winter and on summer weekends at SunWest Park

pick_todo.name: SunWest Park
pick_todo.note: A big county park with a white sand swimming beach, lakes and trails right on the coast.

pick_meet.name: SunWest Park
pick_meet.note: Beach, lakes, trails and an aqua park where people gather on weekends.

pick_meet.name: Hudson Beach strip
pick_meet.note: Sam's, Ollie's, the Inn on the Gulf and the ice cream parlor sit close together, so you see the same faces.

pick_meet.name: Werner Boyce Salt Springs State Park
pick_meet.note: Trails and paddling just south of town, popular with walkers and kayakers.

pick_meet.name: Boating and fishing clubs
pick_meet.note: Hudson's canal life means plenty of clubs, tournaments and dock talk.

name: Port Richey
blurb: A small, unfussy river town where the Pithlachascotee meets the Gulf, built around canals, docks and fishing boats.
day: You run the boat down the Cotee River to the flats in the morning, eat grouper on a deck by the water and watch the sky go orange over the mangroves.
watch: Low lying and mostly in a flood zone, with river and street flooding in big storms like Helene in 2024; US 19 traffic
season: Busier in winter, quiet and steamy in summer

pick_todo.name: Werner Boyce Salt Springs State Park
pick_todo.note: Mangrove paddling, a deep salt spring and quiet trails just south of town.

pick_meet.name: Waterfront Park
pick_meet.note: The city's riverfront park and home to events like Boom on the Bayou, the Fourth of July celebration.

pick_meet.name: Werner Boyce Salt Springs State Park
pick_meet.note: Kayak rentals, trails and a regular crowd of paddlers and birders.

pick_meet.name: Nature Coast Chamber of Commerce
pick_meet.note: Runs local events and mixers in Port Richey and nearby towns.

pick_meet.name: Downtown New Port Richey
pick_meet.note: About ten minutes east, with Sims Park, Main Street and regular outdoor events.

name: Holiday
blurb: A modest, affordable stretch of Pasco coast where canal neighborhoods run out to the Anclote River and the Gulf.
day: You drop the boat at the Anclote River ramp, spend the morning at the Anclote Key sandbars and grab lunch at the Sponge Docks in Tarpon Springs on the way home.
watch: Low coastal neighborhoods west of US 19 flood in surges; the Anclote pier had hurricane damage; US 19 traffic and strip malls
season: Mild winters bring more boaters and anglers; summers are hot and quiet

pick_todo.name: Anclote Key Preserve State Park
pick_todo.note: A barrier island three miles out with an 1887 lighthouse and empty beaches, reached by boat or ferry.

pick_meet.name: Anclote River Park
pick_meet.note: Boat ramp and riverfront park where the boating crowd launches on weekends.

pick_meet.name: Anclote Gulf Park
pick_meet.note: Boardwalk, pier, dog park and picnic shelters where locals fish and watch the sunset.

pick_meet.name: Friends of Anclote Key
pick_meet.note: Volunteer group that runs monthly lighthouse tours on Anclote Key.

pick_meet.name: Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks
pick_meet.note: Ten minutes south, with restaurants, shops and boat tours on the waterfront.

name: Palm Harbor
blurb: A leafy, established town in north Pinellas with an old downtown on the Pinellas Trail and quiet waterfront villages on St. Joseph Sound.
day: You ride the Pinellas Trail to Wall Springs Park in the morning, grab a beer in old downtown at lunch and catch the sunset over the sound from Ozona.
watch: Waterfront pockets like Ozona and Crystal Beach are in flood zones; US 19 traffic; beaches are a short drive, not in town
season: Year round community; busiest in March for golf and winter visitors

pick_todo.name: Wall Springs Park
pick_todo.note: An old spring, a boardwalk and a 35 foot tower with Gulf views, right off the Pinellas Trail.

pick_meet.name: Pinellas Trail
pick_meet.note: The long bike and walking trail that runs through downtown, where riding groups and regulars cross paths every morning.

pick_meet.name: Wall Springs Park
pick_meet.note: Trails, a pier and a lookout tower, connected to the Pinellas Trail.

pick_meet.name: Valspar Championship
pick_meet.note: The PGA tour stop at Innisbrook each spring, a big local tradition.

pick_meet.name: Honeymoon Island State Park
pick_meet.note: The nearest big beach, with trails and a ferry to Caladesi Island.

name: Oldsmar
blurb: A small, tidy city at the top of Old Tampa Bay, with bayfront parks and the fastest airport run in Pinellas.
day: You fish off the long pier at R.E. Olds Park at sunrise, work in Tampa by nine and are back for a paddle at Mobbly Bayou before dinner.
watch: Low areas along upper Old Tampa Bay flood in surges; Tampa Road and Hillsborough Avenue traffic; no Gulf beach
season: Year round; spring festivals and winter racing at Tampa Bay Downs

pick_todo.name: Mobbly Bayou Preserve
pick_todo.note: A 396 acre bayfront preserve with a canoe launch, trails, a fishing pier and an observation platform.

pick_meet.name: Oldsmar Days and Nights
pick_meet.note: The city's big spring festival at R.E. Olds Park, held April 10 to 12 in 2026.

pick_meet.name: R.E. Olds Park
pick_meet.note: Fishing pier, amphitheater, playground and dog area that host most city events.

pick_meet.name: Upper Tampa Bay Oktoberfest
pick_meet.note: A fall festival at Tampa Bay Downs, October 16 to 18 in 2026.

pick_meet.name: Mobbly Bayou Preserve
pick_meet.note: Trails, a canoe launch and a fishing pier on the bay.

name: Belleair Beach
blurb: A small, residential barrier island town on Sand Key, with the Gulf on one side and docks on the Intracoastal on the other.
day: You walk the quiet beach at Morgan Park in the morning, take the boat out from your dock at noon and ride bikes to Indian Rocks Beach for dinner.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 25 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: Barrier island surge and flood risk, hit hard by Helene and Milton in 2024; rebuilding, demolitions and high insurance; most homes in FEMA A or V zones
season: Quiet most of the year; more visitors on nearby beaches in spring

pick_todo.name: Morgan Park
pick_todo.note: The city's beach park with a pavilion, showers and a walkover to the Gulf.

pick_meet.name: Morgan Park
pick_meet.note: The city's beach park with a pavilion and the main public beach access.

pick_meet.name: Bayside Park and Community Center
pick_meet.note: Playground, basketball and the city's fitness classes and gatherings.

pick_meet.name: Belleair Beach Community Foundation
pick_meet.note: Resident group behind local projects like causeway cleanups.

pick_meet.name: Sand Key Park
pick_meet.note: Big county beach park a few minutes north, popular for walks and picnics.

name: Tierra Verde
blurb: A cluster of canal islands at the mouth of Tampa Bay, between St. Pete Beach and Fort De Soto, made for people who live on their boats.
day: You idle out of the canal to Shell Key at breakfast, spend the afternoon at the Fort De Soto beaches and finish with stone crab on the water as the sun sets.
airport: Tampa (TPA) or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 35 to 40 minutes
watch: Low barrier islands with major surge exposure, flooded in Helene and Milton in 2024; one road in and out via the Pinellas Bayway with tolls
season: Busy beach and boat traffic on spring and summer weekends; calm on weekdays

pick_todo.name: Fort De Soto Park
pick_todo.note: Huge county park with some of the best beaches in Florida, a historic fort, trails and a dog beach.

pick_meet.name: Shell Key Preserve
pick_meet.note: Undeveloped island reached by kayak or ferry, a favorite weekend spot for boaters.

pick_meet.name: Fort De Soto Park
pick_meet.note: Beaches, the fishing piers, the dog beach and trails where locals and visitors mix every day.

pick_meet.name: Tampa Bay Watch
pick_meet.note: Nonprofit on the way to Fort De Soto that runs volunteer bay restoration projects.

name: Indian Shores
blurb: A narrow strip of Gulf front condos and beach cottages in the middle of the Pinellas barrier islands, with the Intracoastal on one side and the Gulf a short walk away on the other.
day: You walk the beach at sunrise, stop by the seabird sanctuary to see the pelicans, and end the day with a drink on the sand as the sun drops into the Gulf.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 25 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: Helene and Milton flooded much of the island in 2024 and rebuilding is still uneven; low lying barrier island, storm surge risk, high flood insurance
season: Busy late winter through spring and on summer weekends

pick_todo.name: Seaside Seabird Sanctuary
pick_todo.note: A nonprofit bird hospital on the beach where you can see rescued pelicans and other shorebirds up close.

pick_meet.name: Seaside Seabird Sanctuary
pick_meet.note: The beachfront bird hospital runs on volunteers and donations and holds release days and community events.

pick_meet.name: Redington Shores town events
pick_meet.note: The town next door hosts a picnic, a holiday boat parade and a golf cart parade that anyone nearby can come watch.

pick_meet.name: The beach at sunrise
pick_meet.note: Walkers, shellers and anglers are out early every day, and it is the easiest place to get to know neighbors.

name: Redington Shores
blurb: A small barrier island town with a big public beach park, bay side canal streets full of boat lifts, and a hometown calendar of picnics and holiday parades.
day: You take the boat out from your canal in the morning, spend the afternoon at the beach access park and finish with a casual dinner a short walk up Gulf Boulevard.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 25 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: Heavy Helene and Milton flooding in 2024, many homes demolished or being rebuilt and elevated; storm surge risk and high flood insurance
season: Busy late winter through spring and on summer weekends

pick_todo.name: Redington Shores Beach Access
pick_todo.note: A county beach park with restrooms, showers, a very wide beach and about 170 paid parking spaces.

pick_meet.name: Town Picnic
pick_meet.note: A fall picnic put on by the town and run with volunteer help; the 2026 one was held October 17.

pick_meet.name: Holiday Boat Parade
pick_meet.note: Decorated boats cruise the waterways each December; the 2026 parade is set for December 13.

pick_meet.name: Holiday Golf Cart Parade
pick_meet.note: Neighbors deck out golf carts and roll through town in December.

pick_meet.name: Christmas Tree Lighting at Del Bello Nature Park
pick_meet.note: An early December evening gathering at the town's nature park.

name: North Redington Beach
blurb: A tidy little beach town where resorts and condo towers line the Gulf and quiet single family streets reach out into the bay on narrow fingers of land.
day: You walk out to the Gulf for a morning swim, play tennis at a town park, and watch the sunset from a beach bar at one of the resorts.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 25 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: 2024 Helene and Milton flooding; low lying bay side streets, storm surge risk, high flood insurance and rebuild costs
season: Busy late winter through spring and on summer weekends

pick_todo.name: Gulf Front Park
pick_todo.note: A small town beach park that gives you a public path to the Gulf.

pick_meet.name: Town parks and tennis courts
pick_meet.note: Small neighborhood parks with courts where regulars play and chat.

pick_meet.name: Gulf Front Park
pick_meet.note: The town beach access where morning walkers and swimmers cross paths.

pick_meet.name: Redington Shores holiday parades
pick_meet.note: The town next door hosts a December boat parade and golf cart parade open to anyone nearby.

name: Redington Beach
blurb: A small, almost entirely residential beach town of single family homes, where the streets are quiet and the Gulf is at the end of the block.
day: You bike a few blocks to the beach in the morning, wave to neighbors rebuilding down the street, and grill out on the back porch as the light fades over the bay.
airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 25 minutes; Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
watch: Many homes flooded by Helene and Milton in 2024, some still unpermitted or vacant; storm surge risk, high flood insurance
season: Steady most of the year, a bit busier in spring

pick_todo.name: Liberty and Libations
pick_todo.note: The town's July 4 morning celebration put on by its Parks and Recreation Board.

pick_meet.name: Liberty and Libations
pick_meet.note: A July 4 morning celebration hosted by the Parks and Recreation Board; held July 4, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Town Easter egg hunt
pick_meet.note: A spring event for the community put on by the town.

pick_meet.name: Redington Shores town events
pick_meet.note: The next town north runs picnics and December boat and golf cart parades open to neighbors.

name: Gibsonton
blurb: An old river town on the Alafia where carnival and circus families once wintered, now a growing and affordable South Shore suburb with water close by.
day: You launch a small boat into Bullfrog Creek in the morning, spend the afternoon at the showmen's museum, and catch the sunset over Hillsborough Bay.
watch: Low areas near the Alafia River and Hillsborough Bay flood in big storms; heavy truck and commuter traffic on US 41 and I 75; fast growth
season: Year round, warmer and quieter in summer

pick_todo.name: International Independent Showmen's Museum
pick_todo.note: Two floors of carnival history, including an early Ferris wheel and walk through show trailers, open on weekend afternoons.

pick_meet.name: International Independent Showmen's Museum
pick_meet.note: Open weekend afternoons, and the showmen's clubhouse next door hosts the town's big gatherings.

pick_meet.name: Gibtown Showmen's trade show
pick_meet.note: The carnival industry's big winter trade show, held at the showmen's club grounds.

pick_meet.name: Gibtown Bike Fest
pick_meet.note: A motorcycle rally on the club grounds that brings a crowd each winter.

pick_meet.name: Bullfrog Creek launch
pick_meet.note: A small free ramp where anglers and paddlers trade tips.

name: Miami
blurb: The mainland city on Biscayne Bay, from the towers of Brickell and Edgewater to the shady streets of Coconut Grove and the murals of Wynwood.
day: You grab a cafecito on the way to a run along the bay, work from a cafe in Brickell, then head to the Grove for dinner by the marina.
airport: Miami International (MIA), about 15 to 25 minutes from Brickell
watch: Hurricane exposure, king tide and rain flooding in low streets, heavy traffic, rising condo fees and assessments
season: Busiest December through April, hot and stormy summers

pick_todo.name: The Underline
pick_todo.note: A linear park and trail under the Metrorail tracks running south from Brickell, with courts, gardens and a bike path.

pick_meet.name: Coconut Grove Organic Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays on Grand Avenue in the Grove, a long running local gathering for produce and prepared food.

pick_meet.name: The Underline
pick_meet.note: Group runs, bike rides and free classes happen along the trail under the Metrorail.

pick_meet.name: Coconut Grove Arts Festival
pick_meet.note: A big outdoor art show along the Grove waterfront each February.

pick_meet.name: Dinner Key
pick_meet.note: The marina and nearby sailing clubs are the easiest way into the boating crowd.

name: Jacksonville
blurb: A big, spread out river city where old oak lined neighborhoods like Riverside, Avondale and San Marco sit right on the St. Johns.
day: You walk under the oaks in Avondale for coffee, take the boat out on the St. Johns in the afternoon and end up at a patio in Five Points.
watch: River flooding in low areas during big storms, long drives across a huge city, stadium construction downtown through 2028
season: Mild winters, hot humid summers, busy on game days

pick_todo.name: Riverside Arts Market
pick_todo.note: A Saturday market of local art, food and music under the Fuller Warren Bridge on the river.

pick_meet.name: Riverside Arts Market
pick_meet.note: Saturdays under the Fuller Warren Bridge, with artists, food stands and live music along the river.

pick_meet.name: Jacksonville Jumbo Shrimp
pick_meet.note: The Triple A ballclub plays at the downtown ballpark, and the summer promos make it a social night out.

pick_meet.name: Emerald Trail
pick_meet.note: The S Line and LaVilla Link segments are a good place to join group rides and walks.

pick_meet.name: St. Johns River
pick_meet.note: Rowing clubs, yacht clubs and fishing groups use the river year round.

name: Indian River Shores
blurb: A quiet barrier island town north of Vero Beach, with low rise oceanfront living, big private clubs and the lagoon on the other side.
day: You walk the beach at sunrise, ride the bike path along the island road and head into Vero for dinner on Ocean Drive.
airport: Melbourne (MLB), about 40 minutes. Vero Beach's airport, about 15 minutes, has a few airline flights
watch: Barrier island hurricane and flood exposure, beach erosion and dune repair work, high insurance and club costs

pick_todo.name: Jungle Trail
pick_todo.note: A shady, unpaved historic road along the lagoon, good for a slow bike ride past old groves and hammock.

pick_meet.name: Jungle Trail
pick_meet.note: A historic lagoon side road where walkers, cyclists and birders cross paths most mornings.

pick_meet.name: Captain Forster Hammock Preserve
pick_meet.note: One of the largest remaining coastal hammocks on the island, on Jungle Trail.

pick_meet.name: Ocean Drive in Vero Beach
pick_meet.note: The nearest strip of shops, cafes and restaurants, about ten minutes south.

name: Hutchinson Island
blurb: The long barrier island off Stuart, Jensen Beach and Fort Pierce, with free beach parking, low rise condos and miles of quiet sand.
day: You snorkel the reef at Bathtub Beach in the morning, tour the House of Refuge after lunch and have a drink at the beach tiki bar at sunset.
airport: Palm Beach (PBI), about 50 minutes from the Stuart end
watch: Barrier island hurricane and flood exposure, beach erosion at Bathtub Beach, condo insurance and assessments
season: Busier in winter, turtle nesting in summer

pick_todo.name: House of Refuge Museum
pick_todo.note: Martin County's oldest building, a lifesaving station for shipwrecked sailors set on the rocks above the ocean.

pick_meet.name: Elliott Museum
pick_meet.note: Art, history and vintage cars and boats, with talks and weekly classes in its theater.

pick_meet.name: Stuart Beach
pick_meet.note: Lifeguards, volleyball and basketball courts, rentals and an oceanfront tiki bar at the Seaside Cafe.

pick_meet.name: Florida Oceanographic Coastal Center
pick_meet.note: Trails, aquariums and the stingray and game fish lagoon, with volunteer programs.

pick_meet.name: Jensen Beach Park
pick_meet.note: A free guarded beach where beach yoga groups and volleyball games gather.

name: Sewall's Point
blurb: A small, leafy peninsula town between the St. Lucie and Indian rivers, with deep water lots, quiet streets and the beach one bridge away.
day: You take the boat out from your own dock in the morning, bike the shady road the length of the point and cross the bridge for a sunset swim.
watch: Hurricane and flood exposure on a low peninsula, river water quality after Lake Okeechobee releases, high insurance

pick_todo.name: Sewall's Point Park
pick_todo.note: A small river beach park by the bridge to the island, with shade palms, a gazebo and a butterfly garden.

pick_meet.name: Downtown Stuart
pick_meet.note: Five minutes away for the riverwalk, the green market and restaurants.

pick_meet.name: Sewall's Point Park
pick_meet.note: A riverside park with a playground, gazebo and views of the bridge to the island.

pick_meet.name: The road loop
pick_meet.note: Walkers and cyclists use the road down the point most mornings.

pick_meet.name: Stuart Beach
pick_meet.note: Across the bridge on Hutchinson Island, with lifeguards and a tiki bar.

name: Palm City
blurb: A green, spread out community across the St. Lucie River from Stuart, with canal homes, golf, big sports parks and easy highway access.
day: You fish off the pier at Leighton Park in the morning, catch a game at the park on Mapp Road and meet friends for dinner at a local spot off Martin Downs.
airport: Palm Beach (PBI), about 40 minutes via the Turnpike or Interstate 95
watch: River water quality after Lake Okeechobee releases, hurricane exposure, growing traffic on the bridges

pick_todo.name: Leighton Park
pick_todo.note: A riverside park at the foot of the Palm City Bridge with a fishing pier, boat ramps and a walking path.

pick_meet.name: Jock Leighton Park
pick_meet.note: Skate park, playground and pavilions that host plenty of weekend gatherings.

pick_meet.name: Justin Wilson Memorial Park
pick_meet.note: The big park on Mapp Road, with sports fields, tennis courts, playgrounds, a nature trail and an observation tower.

pick_meet.name: Leighton Park
pick_meet.note: Fishing pier, boat ramps and a river path at the Palm City Bridge.

pick_meet.name: Martin Downs Golf Club
pick_meet.note: Golf and Chipper's restaurant, a common local meeting spot.

name: Port Salerno
blurb: An old fishing village on the Manatee Pocket near the St. Lucie Inlet, with working docks, an artists' district and a waterfront boardwalk.
day: You grab coffee and walk the boardwalk past the fishing boats, run out the inlet for the afternoon and end with dinner on the dock.
watch: Hurricane and flood exposure around the Pocket, river water quality after Lake Okeechobee releases

pick_todo.name: Fish House Art Center
pick_todo.note: Working artist studios and a gallery on the Manatee Pocket, steps from the waterfront boardwalk.

pick_meet.name: Fish House Art Center
pick_meet.note: Five open studios and a gallery on the water, with classes and workshops.

pick_meet.name: Port Salerno Ghost Tours
pick_meet.note: Evening walks through the old fishing village and its stories.

pick_meet.name: Manatee Cove Boat Ramp
pick_meet.note: The public launch where boaters, kayakers and anglers start the day.

pick_meet.name: Twin Rivers Park
pick_meet.note: A waterfront park where people paddle, fish and watch the sunset.

name: Hobe Sound
blurb: A low key village between Stuart and Jupiter, surrounded by a big state park, a wildlife refuge and some of the prettiest beaches on the coast.
day: You paddle the Loxahatchee River in the morning, eat at a local diner and drive under the banyan trees on Bridge Road to the beach for the afternoon.
watch: Hurricane exposure, limited shopping, heavy traffic on Federal Highway in season

pick_todo.name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park
pick_todo.note: About 11,500 acres along the Loxahatchee River, with paddling, biking trails, camping and guided walks.

pick_meet.name: Hobe Sound Farmers Market
pick_meet.note: Every Saturday and Sunday with dozens of vendors, plus seasonal evening markets.

pick_meet.name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park
pick_meet.note: Weekly guided nature walks, monthly nature programs and races like the Treasure Coast Endurance Challenge.

pick_meet.name: Hobe Sound Nature Center
pick_meet.note: Wildlife programs and fishing clinics on the edge of the refuge.

pick_meet.name: Hobe Sound Historical Society
pick_meet.note: Open houses and local history talks through the year.

name: Tequesta
blurb: A small riverfront village at the top of Palm Beach County, where the Loxahatchee River meets the Intracoastal and the beach is a short bridge away.
day: You paddle the Loxahatchee in the morning, snorkel the rocks at Coral Cove Park after lunch and finish with barbecue and a local beer on US 1.
watch: Hurricane exposure, especially oceanfront condos on Beach Road. US 1 traffic in season, and a small village with few shops of its own

pick_todo.name: Coral Cove Park
pick_todo.note: A small beach park on Jupiter Island with limestone rocks, clear water on calm days, and fish and turtles close to shore.

pick_meet.name: The Jupiter sandbar
pick_meet.note: On weekends boats, paddleboards and jet skis gather just past the lighthouse.

pick_meet.name: Village of Tequesta Concert Series
pick_meet.note: Free evening concerts at Constitution Park, with 2026 dates in March, April and May.

pick_meet.name: Lighthouse ArtCenter
pick_meet.note: Galleries, classes and an annual plein air festival on Tequesta Drive.

pick_meet.name: Freedom 4 Miler
pick_meet.note: The village's July 4 morning race, with a one mile run and a kids' run too.

name: Juno Beach
blurb: A small, low key oceanfront town known for its long fishing pier, wide sandy beach and the sea turtles that nest there every summer.
day: You walk the pier at sunrise, bike the path along the ocean, visit the turtle hospital at Loggerhead and end the day back on the sand.
watch: Oceanfront hurricane and erosion exposure, condo insurance and assessments, and strict lighting rules during turtle nesting season
season: Busier in winter, turtle season March through October

pick_todo.name: Loggerhead Marinelife Center
pick_todo.note: A sea turtle hospital and education center with turtle walks and hatchling releases in season.

pick_meet.name: Loggerhead Marinelife Center
pick_meet.note: Turtle hospital with volunteer roles, summer turtle walks and hatchling releases.

pick_meet.name: TurtleFest
pick_meet.note: A free festival at Loggerhead each February with live music, local art and conservation booths.

pick_meet.name: ArtFest by the Sea
pick_meet.note: About 300 artists line the oceanfront road each March; the 2026 show was March 7 and 8.

pick_meet.name: Juno Beach Pier
pick_meet.note: Fishing regulars, sunrise walkers and surfers checking the waves.

name: Lake Park
blurb: A compact, older town on the Intracoastal with a busy public marina, a small downtown on Park Avenue and the inlet just to the south.
day: You launch the boat at the town marina, run out the inlet for a morning of fishing and bring a chair to the sunset celebration at Kelsey Park that evening.
watch: Storm surge along the Intracoastal, US 1 and freight rail noise, and big new waterfront towers changing the skyline

pick_todo.name: Lake Park Harbor Marina
pick_todo.note: A town run marina with 112 slips, two ramps, fuel and overnight trailer parking for Bahamas trips.

pick_meet.name: Sunset Celebration
pick_meet.note: The town's recurring evening event with music and vendors, back at Kelsey Park per an April 2026 town flyer.

pick_meet.name: Lake Park Harbor Marina
pick_meet.note: Slips, ramps and fuel on the Intracoastal, and the place boaters and anglers gather.

pick_meet.name: Kelsey Park
pick_meet.note: A waterfront park on the Intracoastal for walks, picnics and town events.

name: Palm Beach Shores
blurb: An eleven block town at the south tip of Singer Island, wrapped by the ocean, the Palm Beach Inlet and the Intracoastal, with a 1950s beach town feel.
day: You walk to the inlet to watch the boats come in, snorkel or paddle over to Peanut Island and have dinner on the docks at Sailfish Marina.
watch: Barrier island storm and surge exposure, rising prices as older buildings give way to luxury condos, and inlet boat traffic

pick_todo.name: Peanut Island
pick_todo.note: A park island in the inlet with a snorkel lagoon, camping and calm water, a short paddle or boat ride across.

pick_meet.name: Peanut Island
pick_meet.note: Weekend boaters, paddlers and snorkelers meet up on the island's beaches.

pick_meet.name: Sailfish Marina
pick_meet.note: Charters, a waterfront restaurant and a dock bar right on the inlet.

pick_meet.name: Seasiders
pick_meet.note: A longtime local volunteer group active in town life since 1951.

pick_meet.name: The town beach park
pick_meet.note: Morning walks along the ocean and inlet where locals see each other daily.

name: Lake Worth Beach
blurb: An artsy little city with a lively downtown of bungalows and storefronts, a bridge over the lagoon to a classic public beach and pier.
day: You fish off the pier at sunrise, browse the galleries on Lake Avenue, play nine at the city golf course and stay downtown for dinner and live music.
watch: Hurricane exposure, some rough blocks near Dixie Highway and US 1, older homes that need updating, and festival crowds
season: Busiest in winter, festival season February and March

pick_todo.name: Lake Worth Beach Street Painting Festival
pick_todo.note: Hundreds of artists chalk the downtown streets each February; the 2026 festival was February 21 and 22.

pick_meet.name: Lake Worth Beach Street Painting Festival
pick_meet.note: A free two day chalk art festival downtown every February, with music and food.

pick_meet.name: Lake Worth Playhouse
pick_meet.note: A community theater in a historic downtown building on Lake Avenue.

pick_meet.name: July 4 at Bryant Park
pick_meet.note: The city's free celebration with a raft race, live music, a drone show and fireworks.

pick_meet.name: Lake Worth Beach Pier
pick_meet.note: Early morning anglers and sunset walkers on the city's ocean pier.

name: Lantana
blurb: A small, old Florida town on the Intracoastal with a little public beach across the bridge and the state's oldest waterfront restaurant.
day: You launch the kayak at Sportsman's Park, spend the afternoon at Lantana's beach and watch the sunset over the water with a slice of key lime pie.
watch: Storm surge along the Intracoastal, older housing stock, and US 1 and Interstate 95 traffic

pick_todo.name: Old Key Lime House
pick_todo.note: Built in 1889 and known as Florida's oldest waterfront restaurant, right on the Intracoastal.

pick_meet.name: Lantana's public beach
pick_meet.note: Volleyball, picnic tables and a town beach day each spring.

pick_meet.name: Sportsman's Park
pick_meet.note: The town boat ramp and a gathering spot for anglers and paddlers.

pick_meet.name: July 4 at Bicentennial Park
pick_meet.note: The town fireworks celebration on the Intracoastal.

pick_meet.name: Old Key Lime House
pick_meet.note: The town's historic waterfront restaurant and a longtime local meeting place.

name: Boynton Beach
blurb: A big, easygoing city with a busy harbor marina at the inlet, a growing downtown on Ocean Avenue and wetlands to the west.
day: You dive the reef off the inlet on a morning charter, eat lunch on the water by the marina and walk the boardwalk at Green Cay before dinner downtown.
airport: Palm Beach (PBI), about 20 to 25 minutes, or Fort Lauderdale (FLL), about 40 minutes
watch: Hurricane exposure near the water, Interstate 95 and Federal Highway traffic, and new beach parking fees since October 2025

pick_todo.name: Boynton Harbor Marina
pick_todo.note: The jumping off point for dive, fishing and boat rental charters just inside the Boynton Inlet.

pick_meet.name: Boynton Beach Pirate Fest
pick_meet.note: A Halloween weekend festival downtown, set for October 31 and November 1, 2026.

pick_meet.name: Taste of Boynton Beach
pick_meet.note: A spring food event at Centennial Park; the 2026 edition was April 18.

pick_meet.name: Green Cay Nature Center
pick_meet.note: A wetland boardwalk where birders and walkers gather early.

pick_meet.name: Boynton Harbor Marina
pick_meet.note: Dive boats, fishing charters and the regulars who ride them.

name: Vilano Beach
blurb: A small beach community on the north side of the St. Augustine Inlet, with a retro little main street, a fishing pier on the river and downtown St. Augustine just over the bridge.
day: You fish off the Vilano pier at sunrise, spend the afternoon on the wide beach, and drive five minutes over the bridge for dinner in old St. Augustine.
watch: Barrier island flood and hurricane exposure, beach erosion after big storms, bridge traffic into St. Augustine in season
season: Busy summer weekends, easy the rest of the year

pick_todo.name: Vilano Beach Fishing Pier
pick_todo.note: A free, open all night pier on the river side by the inlet, with a small boat dock and the blue bird statue everyone photographs at sunset.

pick_meet.name: Vilano Beach Fishing Pier
pick_meet.note: The center of the community, where anglers swap reports and the fishing tournaments and festivals are based.

pick_meet.name: Old School Kingfish Shootout
pick_meet.note: A June fishing tournament based at the pier. The next one is set for June 11 to 13, 2027.

pick_meet.name: Vilano Beachfront Park
pick_meet.note: The main ocean access on Anahma Drive, where beach festivals and morning walkers gather.

pick_meet.name: GTM Research Reserve
pick_meet.note: Trails, guided walks and volunteer programs a short drive north on A1A.

name: Crescent Beach
blurb: A quiet strip of beach houses and condos south of St. Augustine Beach, between the ocean and the Matanzas River, with one of the widest, calmest beaches on the First Coast.
day: You walk the hard packed sand at low tide in the morning, kayak the Matanzas River after lunch, and watch the sunset over the river from the west side.
airport: Jacksonville (JAX), about 1 hour 10 minutes, or Daytona Beach (DAB), about 1 hour
watch: Barrier island storm exposure, A1A overwash and erosion to the south near Summer Haven and Matanzas Inlet, long drives to airports
season: Quiet most of the year, busier on summer weekends

pick_todo.name: Fort Matanzas National Monument
pick_todo.note: A free ferry ride across the river to a small Spanish fort from the 1740s, plus a beach and a short oak forest trail.

pick_meet.name: Frank Butler Park East
pick_meet.note: Beachfront county park with pavilions and grills where locals gather for cookouts and beach days.

pick_meet.name: Frank Butler Park West
pick_meet.note: The river side park and boat ramp, where anglers and paddlers meet in the morning.

pick_meet.name: Fort Matanzas National Monument
pick_meet.note: Ranger led ferry tours and the river and ocean beaches by the visitor center.

pick_meet.name: Crescent Beach ramp
pick_meet.note: The drive on beach access where a lot of regulars park and set up for the day.

name: Beverly Beach
blurb: One of Florida's tiniest towns, a few blocks wide between the ocean and the Intracoastal just north of Flagler Beach, with an RV resort, beach cottages and homes on canals.
day: You walk across A1A to the beach in the morning, take the boat out on the Intracoastal after lunch, and ride five minutes south for dinner in Flagler Beach.
watch: Beach and dune erosion, a collapsed seawall at the RV resort, A1A storm exposure, beach renourishment construction planned from November 2026

pick_todo.name: Flagler Beach
pick_todo.note: The neighboring beach town five minutes south, with A1A cafes, surf shops and the main strip of restaurants.

pick_meet.name: Flagler Beach A1A strip
pick_meet.note: The closest place for cafes, surf shops and live music, and where most locals from Beverly Beach spend their evenings out.

pick_meet.name: Town commission meetings
pick_meet.note: In a town this small, the monthly meetings are a real way to meet neighbors and get involved.

pick_meet.name: Washington Oaks Gardens State Park
pick_meet.note: Gardens, coquina rock beach and trails a short drive north, popular for walks and volunteering.

pick_meet.name: Intracoastal boat ramps
pick_meet.note: Morning launches in Flagler Beach and Palm Coast where boaters and anglers trade notes.

name: Ormond by the Sea
blurb: A quiet beach community on the barrier island north of Ormond Beach, with small streets of beach cottages between the ocean and the Halifax River and miles of state parks just to the north.
day: You surf fish at North Peninsula State Park in the morning, bike the Ormond Scenic Loop under the oaks, and watch the sunset from the Highbridge Park dock.
watch: A1A washouts in past storms (a new buried seawall was finished around early 2026), hurricane and flood exposure, few shops on the peninsula
season: Quiet most of the year, busier during Daytona event weeks

pick_todo.name: Ormond Scenic Loop
pick_todo.note: A loop of shaded roads along the river, Bulow Creek and the beach, with parks, trails and the centuries old Fairchild Oak.

pick_meet.name: Highbridge Park
pick_meet.note: A small riverside park with a boat ramp, kayak launch and fishing pier where regulars gather.

pick_meet.name: North Peninsula State Park
pick_meet.note: Free beach and trails with the Coastal Strand Trail starting at Smith Creek Landing.

pick_meet.name: Ormond Scenic Loop
pick_meet.note: A popular route for cycling groups, walkers and birders under the oak canopy.

pick_meet.name: Tomoka State Park
pick_meet.note: Camping, kayak rentals and fishing a short drive away, a good spot for group paddles.

name: Holly Hill
blurb: A small, affordable city on the mainland bank of the Halifax River, wedged between Daytona Beach and Ormond Beach, with a riverfront drive, a waterfront park and the beach a bridge away.
day: You grab coffee at Marina Grande, walk Riverside Drive along the Halifax, and cross the bridge for an afternoon on the beach.
watch: Hurricane and river flooding in low areas, event week traffic, an older housing stock in places
season: Steady year round, busier during Daytona event weeks

pick_todo.name: Holly Hill Riverside Market
pick_todo.note: A Sunday market at Sunrise Park on the river, with local vendors from spring through late summer.

pick_meet.name: Holly Hill Riverside Market
pick_meet.note: Sundays 9 to 2 at Sunrise Park on Riverside Drive. The 2026 season ran April 19 through September 13.

pick_meet.name: Sunrise Park
pick_meet.note: The city's riverfront park, home to the market and a nice place for a walk on the Halifax.

pick_meet.name: The Shops at Marina Grande
pick_meet.note: A growing riverfront spot with Dark Alchemy Coffee and more shops opening.

pick_meet.name: Halifax River boat ramps
pick_meet.note: Morning launches where boaters and anglers trade reports.

name: Ponce Inlet
blurb: A small town at the southern tip of the Daytona peninsula, built around a tall red lighthouse, a working fishing harbor and a wide beach that wraps around the inlet.
day: You climb the lighthouse in the morning, fish off the jetty at Lighthouse Point Park, and end the day at a dockside seafood place on the river.
watch: Barrier island hurricane and surge exposure, strong currents near the inlet, one road in and out
season: Busy summer weekends and Daytona event weeks, quiet otherwise

pick_todo.name: Ponce Inlet Lighthouse
pick_todo.note: Florida's tallest lighthouse, with a museum in the old keepers' houses and a 175 foot view over the inlet and river.

pick_meet.name: Ponce Inlet Lighthouse
pick_meet.note: Holiday events and evening programs, like the July 4 celebration on the grounds.

pick_meet.name: Marine Science Center
pick_meet.note: Sea turtle rehab, a free Wildlife Festival each fall and volunteer programs.

pick_meet.name: Lighthouse Point Park
pick_meet.note: The jetty, trails and beach at the tip of the peninsula, where anglers and walkers meet every morning.

pick_meet.name: Hidden Treasure Rum Bar and Grill
pick_meet.note: A shaded waterfront deck that works as an easy local hangout.

name: Edgewater
blurb: A riverfront city on the Indian River Lagoon just south of New Smyrna Beach, with mangrove paddling trails, a long river walk and more house for the money than the beach towns.
day: You paddle the mangrove trails from Menard May Park in the morning, fish the lagoon in the afternoon, and drive 15 minutes to New Smyrna's beach for a sunset swim.
airport: Daytona Beach (DAB), about 30 minutes, or Orlando (MCO), about 1 hour
watch: Repeated neighborhood flooding in Florida Shores (Ian in 2022, Milton in 2024, a rain and king tide flood in Oct 2025), a development pause tied to stormwater, no beach in town

pick_todo.name: Edgewater paddling trails
pick_todo.note: Marked blueway routes through mangrove tunnels on the Indian River Lagoon, with launches at Menard May and Kennedy parks.

pick_meet.name: Menard May Park
pick_meet.note: A riverfront park and paddling launch where kayakers and anglers start their mornings.

pick_meet.name: George R. Kennedy Memorial Park
pick_meet.note: A second lagoon launch point and a nice place for picnics and evening walks.

pick_meet.name: Edgewater River Walk
pick_meet.note: The riverside path along Riverside Drive, busy with walkers, joggers and cyclists.

pick_meet.name: Local fishing guides
pick_meet.note: Lagoon charters that are a fast way to learn the water and meet other anglers.

name: Cape Canaveral
blurb: A small, low key beach city at the north end of the barrier island, between the cruise port and Cocoa Beach, with a quiet beach and launch views from the jetty.
day: You walk the quiet beach in the morning, eat fish on a dock at the Cove for lunch and watch a cruise ship slide out past Jetty Park at sunset.
airport: Orlando (MCO), about 45 minutes, or Melbourne (MLB), about 40
watch: Barrier island hurricane and flood exposure, cruise port traffic on A1A, lots of condos with HOA and insurance costs
season: Busy on cruise days and launch days, calmer than Cocoa Beach year round

pick_todo.name: Jetty Park
pick_todo.note: A beach park and fishing pier at the mouth of Port Canaveral, where cruise ships and rocket launches pass close by.

pick_meet.name: Friday Fest
pick_meet.note: A street festival on Taylor and Poinsetta Avenues on the first Friday of each month except January and July, 6 to 10pm, with food trucks, vendors, beer and wine and live music.

pick_meet.name: Jetty Park
pick_meet.note: Fishing pier, beach and campground at the inlet. On launch nights it fills with people watching the sky.

pick_meet.name: The Cove at Port Canaveral
pick_meet.note: A cluster of waterfront seafood bars and restaurants where locals and charter crews end the day.

pick_meet.name: Carib Brewery taproom
pick_meet.note: A brewery taproom in town that runs tours and tastings.

name: Merritt Island
blurb: A big, leafy island between the Indian and Banana Rivers, full of canal homes and boat docks, with the space center and a huge wildlife refuge at its north end.
day: You take the boat out from your backyard canal in the morning, run errands on Courtenay Parkway after lunch and drive the refuge loop to watch birds at dusk.
airport: Orlando (MCO), about 45 minutes, or Melbourne (MLB), about 35
watch: Low lying land with rain and storm surge flooding in some areas, hurricane exposure, a car dependent layout
season: Steady year round, busier around big launches

pick_todo.name: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge
pick_todo.note: Marsh, lagoon and scrub on the north end of the island, with Black Point Wildlife Drive for birding at sunrise and sunset.

pick_meet.name: Kiwanis Island Park
pick_meet.note: Community center, gym, courts, ballfields, a boat ramp and a fishing dock on Sykes Creek.

pick_meet.name: Brevard Veterans Memorial Center
pick_meet.note: A museum and memorial park that hosts talks and events.

pick_meet.name: Black Point Wildlife Drive
pick_meet.note: A one way birding loop in the refuge, busy with photographers at sunrise and sunset.

pick_meet.name: Boating and fishing clubs
pick_meet.note: With so many docks on the island, local boating and fishing clubs are a common way to meet people.

name: Cocoa Village
blurb: The old brick downtown of Cocoa on the Indian River, with shady streets, pubs, a historic playhouse and a riverfront park that hosts concerts.
day: You walk to coffee and a bakery, browse the shops on Brevard Avenue and end with a beer garden and a concert at the riverfront park.
airport: Orlando (MCO), about 40 minutes, or Melbourne (MLB), about 30
watch: Riverfront flooding and hurricane exposure, limited housing right in the village, prices and condition vary block to block
season: Busy on festival weekends, steady the rest of the year

pick_todo.name: Cocoa Riverfront Park
pick_todo.note: A park and amphitheater on the Indian River at the edge of the village, used for outdoor concerts and festivals.

pick_meet.name: Cocoa Village art and craft fairs
pick_meet.note: Four fairs a year fill the historic streets, including the 40th annual spring fair in 2026 with over 200 artisans.

pick_meet.name: Cocoa Riverfront Park concerts
pick_meet.note: Touring bands on the outdoor stage, with shows on the 2026 calendar into November.

pick_meet.name: Cocoa Village Book Fest
pick_meet.note: A yearly local author festival run by the Main Street group.

pick_meet.name: Historic Cocoa Village Playhouse
pick_meet.note: A restored old theater with community musicals and plays.

name: Rockledge
blurb: A quiet river city just south of Cocoa, known for the oak shaded historic homes along Rockledge Drive and newer neighborhoods toward Viera.
day: You bike Rockledge Drive under the oaks along the river, pick up plants and lunch at Rockledge Gardens and grab dinner at a food truck night in the park.
airport: Orlando (MCO), about 45 minutes, or Melbourne (MLB), about 25
watch: Hurricane exposure and riverfront flooding, older homes with insurance and roof questions, I 95 and US 1 traffic

pick_todo.name: Rockledge Drive
pick_todo.note: A scenic riverside road and historic district with old Florida homes, great for an easy bike ride.

pick_meet.name: Rockledge Gardens
pick_meet.note: A big garden center with a market, workshops and First Friday evenings in summer.

pick_meet.name: Food Truck Friday
pick_meet.note: Regular food truck nights at Larry L. Schultz Park.

pick_meet.name: H.S. Williams House
pick_meet.note: A restored historic house on Rockledge Drive with tours run by a local friends group.

pick_meet.name: Riverwalk Park and Nature Center
pick_meet.note: Boardwalk and trails by the river, a good place to meet other walkers and birders.

name: Indian Harbour Beach
blurb: A small, settled beach town between Satellite Beach and Indialantic, with ocean access on one side, Banana River canals on the other and a big park in the middle.
day: You swim laps at the park pool, paddle the Banana River from Bicentennial Park and walk over to the beach for the sunset glow on the water.
airport: Melbourne (MLB), about 15 minutes, or Orlando (MCO), about 1 hour
watch: Barrier island hurricane and flood exposure, canal homes need flood insurance

pick_todo.name: Gleason Park
pick_todo.note: A 27 acre park with a lake, a heated pool open year round, walking paths and the town recreation center.

pick_meet.name: Art and Crafts Show
pick_meet.note: Held at Gleason Park on the third Saturday in November.

pick_meet.name: Gleason Park Recreation Center
pick_meet.note: Pool, shuffleboard, a walking loop and community programs.

pick_meet.name: Christmas in the Park
pick_meet.note: Tree lighting on the lake with caroling, held each December.

pick_meet.name: Algonquin Sports Complex
pick_meet.note: Baseball, softball and soccer fields where league games bring people together.

name: Melbourne
blurb: The Space Coast's main mainland city on the Indian River, with two walkable old downtowns, an arts district, its own airport and the beach 15 minutes away.
day: You grab breakfast in downtown Melbourne, walk the Eau Gallie Arts District in the afternoon and cross the causeway for a swim before dinner by the river.
airport: Melbourne (MLB), about 10 minutes, or Orlando (MCO), about 1 hour
watch: Hurricane exposure, riverfront flooding, traffic on Wickham Road and US 1, a spread out city beyond the old downtowns

pick_todo.name: Eau Gallie Arts District
pick_todo.note: A historic riverside district of murals, galleries and the Foosaner Art Museum, with a First Friday art night.

pick_meet.name: EGAD First Friday
pick_meet.note: Artists and makers set up along Highland Avenue on the first Friday of each month, 5:30 to 8:30pm.

pick_meet.name: Foosaner Art Museum
pick_meet.note: Florida Tech's art museum in Eau Gallie, with free jazz nights during First Friday in past seasons.

pick_meet.name: Downtown Melbourne street festivals
pick_meet.note: New Haven Avenue closes for festivals through the year.

pick_meet.name: Brevard Zoo
pick_meet.note: A large zoo with kayak trips and a treetop course, and a popular place for members to meet up.
